summary: This Part II extends Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves beyond schemes of finite type over a field or a one-dimensional base. Following Gabber's work as written in Illusie–Laszlo–Orgogozo, it plans the topology of ℓ′-alterations, the Cohen–Gabber theorem and partial algebraization, Gabber's weak and prime-to-ℓ local uniformization, oriented products and oriented cohomological descent, Gabber's finiteness theorem for quasi-excellent schemes, dimension functions, the affine Lefschetz theorem and the cohomological dimension bound, and dualizing complexes on excellent schemes with Gabber's duality theorem and local duality. It ends with the local results of Česnavičius–Scholze: local absolute purity, the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem in local étale cohomology, and the algebraic tilting of étale cohomology of henselian perfectoid pairs.

nodes.title: The category alt/S of maximally finite dominant schemes
nodes.statement: Let S be a noetherian scheme and ℓ a prime, the integer 1 or the symbol ∞ (with ℓ′ the set of positive integers prime to ℓ, and ∞′ = {1}). A morphism f : X → Y is maximally dominant if it sends every maximal point (generic point of an irreducible component) of X to a maximal point of Y; it is maximally ℓ′-finite if for every maximal point η of X the extension κ(η)/κ(f(η)) is finite and every maximal point μ of Y in the image of f has a maximal point η above it with [κ(η) : κ(μ)] ∈ ℓ′ (maximally finite when ℓ = 1, where the second condition is empty). alt/S is the category whose objects are reduced S-schemes of finite type whose structure map is maximally finite and maximally dominant, with S-morphisms as morphisms. For X of finite type over S, X^md is the closure of the image of the generic fibre X ×_S η_S with its reduced structure (the union of the irreducible components of X dominating a component of S). Fibre products in alt/S are X ×^alt_S Y := (X ×_S Y)^md.
hypotheses: S noetherian; objects reduced and of finite type over S.
Maximal dominance is the notion of AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.0/maximally-dominating; ℓ′-finiteness at maximal points refines its ℓ′-alterations to non-proper morphisms.
proofSteps: Define the subcategory and the functor T ↦ T^md on finite-type S-schemes; T^md is right adjoint to the inclusion of reduced maximally dominant finite-type S-schemes (ILO II 1.2.5).
Existence of fibre products in alt/S: apply (−)^md to the ordinary fibre product and use the adjunction (ILO II 1.2.6).
Every morphism of alt/S is maximally finite dominant (ILO II 1.1.10), and S_red is final (ILO II 1.2.3).
acceptance: The ordinary fibre product of two copies of the blow-up of 𝔸² at the origin over 𝔸² is not maximally dominant; its md part is the fibre product in alt/𝔸².
For integral S and integral X, an object X → S of alt/S that is proper and surjective is an alteration in the sense of AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.0/alteration.

uses.how: the topology of ℓ′-alterations is a Grothendieck topology on alt/S
hypercoverings for the alteration topology are simplicial objects of alt/X
base changes of hypercovers are replaced by their md parts

tests.name: AltCat.test_final
tests.statement: For S = Spec k with k a field, S is final in alt/S and every object is finite over k: it is reduced of finite type and its maximal points have residue fields finite over k, so it has dimension zero.

tests.name: AltCat.test_blowup_product
tests.statement: For S = 𝔸²_k and X = Bl_0 𝔸², the ordinary fibre product X ×_S X has an irreducible component over the exceptional locus that does not dominate S; X ×^alt_S X is the closure of the diagonal generic part.

tests.name: AltCat.test_closed_point_not_object
tests.statement: For S = 𝔸¹_k, the inclusion of the origin is of finite type and reduced but not maximally dominant, so it is not an object of alt/S.

tests.name: AltCat.test_alteration_compat
tests.statement: For S integral and X → S proper, surjective and integral, X is an object of alt/S exactly when X → S is an alteration (PA.0/alteration).

tests.name: AltCat.test_affine_line_not_object
tests.statement: For S = Spec k, T = 𝔸¹_k has T^md = T but is not in alt/S: its generic field k(t) is not finite over k. Taking the md part does not impose generic finiteness.

nodes.title: The topology of ℓ′-alterations
nodes.statement: Let S be noetherian and ℓ as in EQ.0/alteration-category. An étale covering (X_i → X) is ℓ′-decomposed if every point x of X lifts to a point x_i of some X_i with [κ(x_i) : κ(x)] ∈ ℓ′ (for ℓ = 1 an ordinary étale covering, for ℓ = ∞ a Nisnevich covering). The topology alt_ℓ′ of ℓ′-alterations on alt/S is the Grothendieck topology generated by (i) ℓ′-decomposed étale coverings and (ii) single morphisms that are proper, surjective and maximally ℓ′-finite. alt_1′ is the alteration topology alt. A hypercovering for alt_ℓ′ of X is a simplicial object X_• of alt/X with X_0 → X an alt_ℓ′-covering and whose maps X_{n+1} → (cosk_n X_•)_{n+1} are alt_ℓ′-coverings.
hypotheses: The generating families are not closed under composition (ILO II 2.3.2); the topology is the one they generate.
Condition (i) is imposed at every point, condition (ii) only at maximal points.
proofSteps: Check that the families (i) and (ii) are stable under base change in alt/S (ILO II 1.2.7, 2.1.1) and define the generated topology (ILO II 2.3.1).
Flat base change of coverings along S′ → S with S′ locally noetherian (ILO II 2.3.4).
Hypercoverings are defined as for any site, following Deligne's construction (Hodge III §5–6).
acceptance: Spec ℤ[i] → Spec ℤ is an alt_ℓ′-covering for every odd prime ℓ and is not an alt_2′-covering.
A dense open immersion U ⊊ X is not an alt-covering.

uses.how: the uniformization theorems produce alt and alt_ℓ′ coverings by regular schemes with snc boundary
oriented cohomological descent is proved along alt hypercoverings
the finiteness theorem uses the standard form of alt_ℓ′ coverings

tests.name: AltTopology.test_gaussian_odd
tests.statement: For ℓ odd, the finite flat map Spec ℤ[i] → Spec ℤ of generic degree 2 is proper, surjective and maximally ℓ′-finite, hence alt_ℓ′-covering.

tests.name: AltTopology.test_gaussian_two
tests.statement: Spec ℤ[i] → Spec ℤ is not alt_2′-covering: every alt_2′-covering of Spec ℤ has, over the generic point, a point whose residue field has odd degree over ℚ, and no such field contains ℚ(i).

tests.name: AltTopology.test_ell_one
tests.statement: For ℓ = 1 the condition on degrees is empty, so every proper surjective generically finite map of integral schemes is alt-covering (e.g. Frobenius of 𝔸¹ over 𝔽_p).

tests.name: AltTopology.test_open_not_cover
tests.statement: The inclusion 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹ is not an alt-covering of 𝔸¹: the origin is not in the image of any refinement.

tests.name: AltTopology.test_nisnevich

sources.match: Defines ℓ′-decomposed étale coverings and the topology of ℓ′-alterations generated by them and by proper surjective maximally ℓ′-finite maps; alt is the case ℓ = 1; coverings are stable under flat base change.

nodes.title: Standard forms of alteration coverings
nodes.statement: Let X be irreducible, noetherian and quasi-excellent, and ℓ a prime. (1) Every alt_ℓ′-covering family of X is refined by a family (V_i → Y → X)_i in which Y is integral, Y → X is proper, surjective, of generic degree prime to ℓ, and (V_i → Y)_i is a Nisnevich covering; for ℓ = 1 one may take (V_i → Y) a Zariski covering. (2) Every alt_ℓ′-covering family of X is refined by a family (W_i → V_i → Y → X)_i of irreducible schemes in which Y → X is a proper birational modification, (V_i → Y) is a Nisnevich covering and each W_i → V_i is finite, flat and of degree prime to ℓ. For reducible X apply (2) to the disjoint union of the irreducible components.
hypotheses: X noetherian, irreducible, quasi-excellent (quasi-excellence is used for the reduction; ILO II 3.2.1 expects it to be superfluous).
proofSteps: Étale case: an ℓ′-decomposed étale covering is dominated by a Nisnevich covering of a finite maximally ℓ′-finite surjective Y → X; pass to a normal limit with pro-ℓ absolute Galois group, where ℓ′-decomposed étale maps are completely decomposed (ILO II 3.1.1).
Proper case and composition: combine (i) and (ii) using the exchange of a finite flat map of degree prime to ℓ with a Nisnevich covering after henselization (ILO II 3.2.1–3.2.3).
Flatten Y → X by an admissible blow-up (Raynaud–Gruson; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.0/finite-type-flattening) to obtain the birational-then-finite-flat form (2).
acceptance: For X = Spec of a henselian local ring and a covering by a single finite flat map of degree prime to ℓ, form (2) is the map itself with Y = X.
The standard form of a Zariski covering is itself (Y = X).

sources.locator: Exposé II, Proposition 3.1.1, Théorèmes 3.2.1 and 3.2.3, pp. 28–31 (printed)
sources.match: Every covering for the ℓ′-alteration topology of an irreducible quasi-excellent scheme is refined by a proper surjective generic-degree-prime-to-ℓ map followed by a Nisnevich covering, or by a modification, a Nisnevich covering and finite flat maps of degree prime to ℓ.

nodes.title: Valuative characterisation of alteration coverings
nodes.statement: Let X be noetherian and Y → X an object of alt/X. Then Y → X is a covering for the alteration topology if and only if every maximally dominant morphism Spec V → X, with V a valuation ring whose fraction field is algebraically closed, lifts to a morphism Spec V → Y. The analogue for alt_ℓ′ replaces the algebraically closed fraction field by a perfect field whose absolute Galois group is a pro-ℓ group (the quotient of the geometric generic point by an ℓ-Sylow subgroup).
hypotheses: X noetherian; V ranges over valuation rings with the stated fraction fields; the map Spec V → X is maximally dominant.
proofSteps: Necessity: proper surjective generators lift over a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field by the valuative criterion and lifting of the generic point; an étale cover lifts because such a valuation ring is strictly henselian (ILO II 4.2.1).

Sufficiency: normalize integral components, use the quasi-compact Riemann–Zariski space to select finitely many local lifts, and descend these lifts from the algebraic closure of the generic field to a finite extension and a proper modification. Their finite open covering gives an alteration refinement (published ILO II 4.2.1, pp. 33–34). This argument does not assume quasi-excellence.
For the prime-to-ℓ variant use the fixed field of an ℓ-Sylow subgroup of the absolute Galois group and the same argument, as in II 4.2.2.
acceptance: The open immersion 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹ fails the criterion: a valuation ring centred at the origin does not lift; Spec ℤ[i] → Spec ℤ satisfies it for alt.
For X the spectrum of a DVR, the normalisation of X in a finite extension of its fraction field is an alteration covering; the criterion reduces to the extension of valuations.

sources.locator: Exposé II, Théorème 4.2.1 and Remarque 4.2.2, p. 32 (printed), after Goodwillie–Lichtenbaum, Theorem 3.5
sources.match: An object of alt/X is an alteration covering exactly when it is valuatively surjective for valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field; the prime-to-ℓ variant uses pro-ℓ Galois groups.

sources.locator: Théorème 4.2.1 and Remarque 4.2.2, pp. 33–34
sources.match: The published statement uses an algebraically closed fraction field; its Riemann–Zariski proof covers noetherian bases without quasi-excellence.

nodes.title: Approximation of schemes over a complete local ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an excellent henselian noetherian local ring with completion Â, S = Spec A, Ŝ = Spec Â, and write Ŝ = lim_α S_α with S_α smooth over S (Popescu). Let X be of finite type over Ŝ with a model X_{α0} over S_{α0}. There are α1 ≥ α0 and integers n0 ≥ c > 0 such that for every n ≥ n0, α ≥ α1 and every section u of S_α → S that is (n+1)-close to the canonical map Ŝ → S_α, the pulled-back scheme X_u over S is (n+1−c)-isomorphic to X above the closed fibre (an approximation of order n − c). If X and Y are a-close at a point x of their common closed fibre, then (i) for a ≥ 1 they have the same dimension at x, and (ii) for a ≥ 2, X is regular at x iff Y is; (iii) if X is regular, every sufficiently fine approximation X_u is regular in an open neighbourhood of its closed fibre.
hypotheses: A excellent henselian noetherian local. For the closed-fibre ideals I and J, an a-isomorphism identifies the (a−1)-st infinitesimal fibres and the graded algebras gr^a_n = I^n/I^{n+a} and J^n/J^{n+a} for all integer n, taking I^n = O for n ≤ 0 (ILO III 4.2, p. 39). Agreement of a truncated ordinary associated graded alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Popescu's theorem writes the regular map A → Â as a filtered colimit of smooth A-algebras (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.15, Néron–Popescu desingularization).

Artin approximation gives sections u of S_α → S close to the canonical map; compare graded pieces gr^n of X and X_u via the Tougeron–type estimate of ILO III Proposition 4.5 to obtain the (n+1−c)-isomorphism (ILO III 5.1).
Dimension and regularity are read from the normal cone and the Zariski tangent space, which are determined by low-order graded pieces (ILO III Corollaire 5.4).
acceptance: For X = Ŝ itself, every approximation X_u is S, and the closed fibres agree to all orders.

For X = Spec Â[t]/(t² − a) with a a unit and 2 invertible, the approximations Spec A[t]/(t² − a_u) with a_u close to a are étale over S. If A is also regular they are regular; étaleness alone does not make a singular base regular.

sources.locator: Exposé III, Définition 4.2, Théorème 5.1, Définition 5.2 and Corollaire 5.4, pp. 39, 41–43 (printed)
sources.match: States the approximation theorem for finite-type schemes over the completion of an excellent henselian local ring and the comparison of dimension and regularity for schemes that are close to sufficient order.

nodes.title: Reduction of uniformization to local henselian excellent normal schemes
nodes.statement: Consider the uniformization statement U(X): for every nowhere dense closed Z ⊂ X there is a finite family (X_i → X) covering for alt (resp. alt_ℓ′, ℓ invertible on X) with each X_i regular and connected and each preimage of Z the support of a strict normal crossings divisor (possibly empty). If U(X) holds for every noetherian local henselian excellent normal scheme X (resp. of dimension ≤ d), then U(X) holds for every noetherian quasi-excellent scheme X (resp. of dimension ≤ d).
hypotheses: Z nowhere dense (rare) closed; snc supports in the sense of AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.0/snc-support.
proofSteps: Normalisation is an alt_ℓ′-covering and preserves rareness of Z, so reduce to X normal integral.

For x ∈ X the henselisation X_(x) is excellent (EGA IV 18.7.6; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21) with Z_(x) rare; a uniformizing family over X_(x) is dominated by a standard covering (EQ.0/standard-form-covers) which spreads out to an étale neighbourhood of x by limit arguments.
Noetherian induction and quasi-compactness assemble the local families (ILO II 4.1.1–4.1.2, 4.3.3).
acceptance: For X regular with Z an snc support, U(X) holds with the identity family and the reduction is trivial.
The dimension bound is preserved: a family produced for X of dimension ≤ d uses only local schemes of dimension ≤ d.

sources.locator: Exposé II, Théorèmes 4.3.1–4.3.2 and Proposition 4.3.3, p. 33 (printed)
sources.match: States Gabber's weak and prime-to-ℓ uniformization theorems and proves that each follows from its case of local henselian excellent normal schemes, with the dimension bound kept.

nodes.title: Reduction of uniformization to complete local rings
nodes.statement: If the uniformization statement U(T) of EQ.0/uniformization-henselian-reduction (for alt, resp. alt_ℓ′ with ℓ invertible) holds for every noetherian complete local scheme T, then it holds for every noetherian quasi-excellent scheme T.
hypotheses: Uniformization for complete local rings is assumed in the relevant topology; ℓ invertible for the prime-to-ℓ version.
proofSteps: By EQ.0/uniformization-henselian-reduction reduce to T local, excellent and henselian (a henselian quasi-excellent local scheme is excellent).

Uniformize the completion T̂; approximate the finitely many regular schemes and snc divisors of the family by models over T using EQ.0/artin-popescu-approximation, keeping regularity near the closed fibre and the combinatorics of the divisors.
Check the approximated family is still covering using the standard forms (EQ.0/standard-form-covers) and the valuative criterion.
acceptance: For T complete the statement is the hypothesis itself.
For T = Spec of the henselisation of 𝔸²_k at the origin and Z = V(xy(x − y)), the family produced from the blow-up of the completion descends to the blow-up of T.

sources.locator: Exposé III, Théorème 6.1 and Proposition 6.2, p. 43 (printed)
sources.match: States the uniformization theorem for the alteration and ℓ′-alteration topologies and proves that its case of noetherian complete local schemes implies the general quasi-excellent case.

nodes.title: The Cohen–Gabber theorem in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete noetherian local ring of equal characteristic p > 0 that is reduced and equidimensional of dimension d, with residue field k. There is a subring A_0 ⊆ A isomorphic to k⟦t_1, …, t_d⟧ such that A is finite and torsion-free over A_0 and generically étale over it (étale over a dense open of Spec A_0), and A_0 → A induces an isomorphism on residue fields.
hypotheses: Equal characteristic p > 0 (in characteristic 0 Cohen's theorem with separable Noether normalisation already gives the conclusion).
Equidimensional: every minimal prime 𝔭 has dim A/𝔭 = d.
proofSteps: Choose a p-basis of k and lift it; this determines a coefficient field κ ⊂ A (Cohen's structure theorem, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1).
Show that for a suitable choice of the lifts the completed module of differentials Ω̂¹_{A/κ} has generic rank d on every irreducible component (ILO IV 2.1.4–2.1.11).
Choose parameters t_1, …, t_d whose differentials span generically; then A is finite over κ⟦t⟧ and generically étale (ILO IV 2.1.12).
acceptance: For A = k⟦x, y⟧/(y² − x³) with p ≠ 2, 3, A_0 = k⟦x⟧ works: A is free of rank 2 over it and étale where x ≠ 0.
For A = 𝔽_p(s)⟦x⟧ with s transcendental, A_0 = A with t_1 = x; the naive choice k⟦x^p⟧ is finite but not generically étale.

sources.locator: Exposé IV, Théorème 2.1.1 and its proof §§2.1.3–2.1.12, pp. 50–53 (printed); Gabber 2005a, Lemma 8.1
sources.match: Every complete noetherian local reduced equidimensional ring of equal characteristic p is finite, torsion-free and generically étale over a power series subring in dim A variables with the same residue field.

nodes.title: Equivariant Cohen–Gabber theorem
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete noetherian local reduced ring of equal characteristic, of dimension d, with residue field κ, and let a finite group G act on A with |G| invertible in κ. There is a G-equivariant finite generically étale morphism κ⟦t_1, …, t_d⟧ → A, where κ → A lifts the identity of κ and G acts trivially on the t_i. Here generic étaleness means étaleness over a dense open of the power-series target; lower-dimensional components of Spec A can disappear over that open.
hypotheses: |G| invertible in κ; equal characteristic (A contains a field).
proofSteps: Set B = A^G and λ = κ^G; B is complete local noetherian and A is finite over B (ILO IV 2.2.3). Its dimension is d, but B need not be equidimensional.

Let I be the intersection of the minimal primes of B having dimension d. Apply the non-equivariant theorem to the reduced equidimensional quotient B/I (or Cohen structure in characteristic zero). Lift its coefficient field and parameters to B, as in IV 2.2.4–2.2.5, obtaining a finite parametrization generically étale over its target.

Extend λ to the finite separable residue extension κ, lift this extension étale-locally with its G-action, and map κ⟦t_1,…,t_d⟧ equivariantly into A. The generic field extensions of A over the invariants are separable; the resulting parametrization is finite and étale over a dense target open (IV 2.2.6, pp. 54–55).
acceptance: For G trivial and A equidimensional in positive characteristic, this is the non-equivariant theorem; the general reduced case uses its maximal-dimensional quotient.
For A = k⟦x⟧ with G = μ_2 acting by x ↦ −x (char k ≠ 2), one can take t = x²: the map k⟦t⟧ → A is finite, equivariant and étale where x ≠ 0.

sources.locator: Exposé IV, Théorème 2.2.2 and §§2.2.3–2.2.6, pp. 53–55 (printed)
sources.match: Gives a G-equivariant finite generically étale power-series parametrisation of a complete local reduced equicharacteristic ring when the order of G is invertible.

nodes.title: Epp's theorem on eliminating wild ramification
nodes.statement: Let T → S be a local dominant morphism of complete traits of residue characteristic p > 0, with residue fields κ_S perfect and the maximal perfect subfield of κ_T algebraic over κ_S. There is a finite extension of traits S′ → S such that the normalisation of the reduced fibre product, T′ = ((T ×_S S′)_red)^norm, has reduced special fibre over S′. In mixed characteristic T ×_S S′ is already reduced.
hypotheses: Complete traits; κ_S perfect; the perfect part of κ_T algebraic over κ_S.
proofSteps: Epp's proof (Invent. Math. 19 (1973), Theorem 1.9) reduces to the case of a ramified Artin–Schreier tower and kills wild ramification by a suitable finite extension of the base; ILO IV §3 records the statement and the sorites used.
Remark: in mixed characteristic the fibre product is flat over S′ with reduced generic fibre, hence reduced (ILO IV Remarque 3.1.3).

The equal-characteristic p-cyclic step must include Kuhlmann’s correction: transformed Artin–Schreier terms can acquire equal exponents and cancel, so iterate after recombination until the finite set of offending coefficients shrinks to the required case (K10, pp. 1–3). This does not replace reading Epp’s remaining proof; gap EPP-1973 stays open.
acceptance: If T → S is unramified with separable residue field extension, S′ = S works.
In mixed characteristic T ×_S S′ is reduced, so only normalisation is needed (ILO IV Remarque 3.1.3).

sources.locator: Exposé IV, Théorème 3.1.2 and Remarque 3.1.3, p. 55 (printed), citing Epp 1973, Theorem 1.9
sources.match: States Epp's theorem: after a finite extension of the base trait, the normalised reduced base change of a dominant map of complete traits has reduced special fibre.

sources.locator: pp. 1–3, correction to the equal-characteristic case of Epp’s Theorem 1.3
sources.match: Repairs the possible cancellation of leading Artin–Schreier terms by iteration; the main elimination theorem survives.

nodes.title: The Cohen–Gabber theorem in mixed characteristic, prime to ℓ
nodes.statement: Let X = Spec A be a complete noetherian local normal scheme of dimension d ≥ 2 with residue field k of characteristic p > 0 and generic point of characteristic 0. (1) There are a finite surjective X′ → X with X′ normal integral of residue field k′, and a finite surjective X′ → Spec V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−1}⟧ with V a discrete valuation ring of residue field k′, étale over a p-dense open (an open meeting the fibre over p densely). (2) For a prime ℓ ≠ p there are a normal integral local Y with an action of a finite ℓ-group H and an H-equivariant finite surjective Y → X with Y/H → X of generic degree prime to ℓ, a complete mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring V with residue field that of Y and a compatible H-action, and an H-equivariant local finite morphism Y → Spec V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−1}⟧, étale over a p-dense open, with H acting trivially on the t_i.
hypotheses: d ≥ 2; mixed characteristic (0, p); ℓ ≠ p in (2).
proofSteps: Use Cohen rings and Cohen's structure theorem to map X to Spec W(k_0) with k_0 the maximal perfect subfield of k (ILO IV 4.1.7–4.1.8, 4.2.3).
At each generic point of the fibre over p, eliminate wild ramification with Epp's theorem (EQ.1/epp-theorem) after a finite base change.

Choose parameters giving a finite map to V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−1}⟧ that is étale over a p-dense open (ILO IV 4.2.2); for (2) replace the base extension by its Galois closure and descend along an ℓ-Sylow subgroup (ILO IV 4.3.1).
acceptance: For X = Spec ℤ_p⟦x⟧ (d = 2), V = ℤ_p and t_1 = x with X′ = X work in (1).
In (2) with H trivial, Y → X itself must have generic degree prime to ℓ.

sources.locator: Exposé IV, Théorèmes 4.2.2 and 4.3.1, pp. 58–60 (printed)
sources.match: In mixed characteristic a complete local normal ring becomes, after a finite (prime-to-ℓ up to an ℓ-group action) extension, finite and p-generically étale over a power series ring over a complete discrete valuation ring.

nodes.title: Partially algebraizable complete local rings
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete noetherian local ring and (I_e)_{e∈E} a family of ideals of A. The pair (A, (I_e)) is partially algebraizable if there exist a complete noetherian local ring B with dim B < dim A, a B-algebra C of finite type, a maximal ideal 𝔫 of C above the maximal ideal of B, and an isomorphism A ≅ Ĉ_𝔫 (completion of the localisation) under which every I_e is the extension of an ideal of C_𝔫.
hypotheses: A complete noetherian local; E arbitrary (in the theorems, finite).
proofSteps: Definition; closure under finite intersections of ideals (ILO V 2.2.1) and under primary decomposition is part of the API.
acceptance: A = k⟦x, y⟧ with I = (y − x²) is partially algebraizable with B = k⟦x⟧, C = B[y], 𝔫 = (x, y).
A field is never partially algebraizable (dim B < 0 is impossible).

uses.how: the partial algebraization theorems produce such presentations
the complete local scheme to be uniformized is realised as the completion of a curve over a regular base of dimension d − 1, to apply de Jong's theorem
the duality theorem is proved by induction on dimension using V 3.1.3

tests.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.test_power_series
tests.statement: A = k⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧ (d ≥ 1) with the ideals (x_1), …, (x_d) is partially algebraizable over B = k⟦x_1, …, x_{d−1}⟧, C = B[x_d], 𝔫 = (x_1, …, x_d).

tests.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.test_field
tests.statement: A field k with any family of ideals is not partially algebraizable, since no complete local B has dimension < 0.

tests.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.test_graph
tests.statement: In A = k⟦x,y⟧ the ideal (y − x²) is extended from C_𝔫 for C = k⟦x⟧[y] and 𝔫 = (x,y). More generally the same presentation works for (y − f(x)) with any f(x) ∈ k⟦x⟧.

tests.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.test_not_finite_type_over_A
tests.statement: The trivial presentation B = A, C = A is not allowed: it violates dim B < dim A.

api.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable
api.statement: The predicate on a complete local ring with a family of ideals.

api.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.of_iso
api.statement: Invariance under isomorphisms of complete local rings carrying the ideals.

api.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.inter
api.statement: If the family (I_e) is partially algebraizable, so is the family enlarged by I_i ∩ I_j for any two indices, with the same presentation: completion of the noetherian local ring C_𝔫 is flat, so extension of ideals commutes with finite intersections. With primary decomposition this reduces families to primary ideals (ILO V 2.2.1).

api.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.dim_lt
api.statement: Every presentation has dim B < dim A.

api.name: PartiallyAlgebraizable.geometric
api.statement: Equivalently Spec A is the completion at a closed point of the closed fibre of a finite-type scheme over a complete noetherian local base of smaller dimension, with each V(I_e) induced from a closed subset. Under the reduced equal-characteristic or normal mixed-characteristic hypotheses of V 3.1.3–3.1.4, the algebraization theorems give a regular base of dimension dim A − 1, after the stated finite prime-to-ℓ extension in mixed characteristic; regularity is an extra theorem, not part of this equivalence.

sources.locator: Exposé V, §2.1.1, p. 64 (printed)
sources.match: Defines a complete noetherian local ring with a collection of ideals to be partially algebraizable when it is the completion of a finite-type algebra over a complete local ring of smaller dimension at a maximal ideal over the closed point, with the ideals coming from that algebra.

nodes.title: Partial algebraization in equal characteristic
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete noetherian local reduced ring of equal characteristic which is not a field. Then for every finite family of ideals (I_e), the pair (A, (I_e)) is partially algebraizable.
hypotheses: A reduced, equal characteristic, dim A ≥ 1; finitely many ideals.
proofSteps: Reduce to primary ideals (EQ.1/partially-algebraizable, intersection property).
Use EQ.1/cohen-gabber-equal-characteristic (or EQ.1/cohen-gabber-equivariant with G = 1 when A is not equidimensional) to get a finite generically étale X → X_0 = Spec k⟦t_1, …, t_d⟧.

Minimal primes are handled by generic étaleness; lower-dimensional supports lie over V(g) for a g ∈ k⟦t⟧ − 0; after a Weierstrass change of coordinates make g a Weierstrass polynomial in t_d and algebraize along k⟦t_1, …, t_{d−1}⟧[t_d] using Elkik's theorem on finite étale algebras over henselian pairs (ILO V 1.1.1, 1.1.3, 1.2.4, 2.2).
acceptance: For A = k⟦x, y⟧/(xy) (dimension 1) and the ideals (x), (y), one may take B = k, C = k[x, y]/(xy) and 𝔫 = (x, y).
The hypothesis 'not a field' is needed by EQ.1/partially-algebraizable's degenerate test.

sources.locator: Exposé V, Théorème 2.1.2 and §2.2, pp. 64–66 (printed)
sources.match: A complete noetherian local reduced equicharacteristic ring that is not a field, together with any finite family of ideals, is partially algebraizable.

nodes.title: Partial algebraization prime to ℓ in mixed characteristic
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete noetherian local normal ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) and dimension d ≥ 2, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. There is a finite injective A → A′ of generic degree prime to ℓ with A′ normal integral such that every finite family of ideals of A′ is partially algebraizable. Geometrically: for a complete noetherian local normal X of mixed characteristic and dimension d ≥ 2, finitely many closed subsets Z_i ⊂ X and ℓ invertible on X, there are a complete regular local scheme S of mixed characteristic and dimension d − 1, a local normal X′ with a finite π : X′ → X of generic degree prime to ℓ, a finite-type f : Y → S and an isomorphism a of X′ with the completion of Y at a closed point of its special fibre, and closed F_i ⊂ Y with π^{-1}(Z_i) = a^{-1}(F_i). For X reduced of equal characteristic and not a field, the analogous presentation over a complete regular local base of dimension dim X − 1 holds with X′ = X (V 3.1.4).
hypotheses: Mixed characteristic (0, p), d ≥ 2, ℓ ≠ p; finitely many closed subsets.
proofSteps: Apply EQ.1/cohen-gabber-mixed-characteristic (2) to get B_0 = V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−1}⟧ → B with an ℓ-group H, and set A′ = B^H (ILO V 3.2.1).
Algebraize ideals of A′ along V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−2}⟧[t_{d−1}] by the Weierstrass and Elkik arguments of the equal-characteristic case, keeping track of the H-action (ILO V 3.2.2 onwards).
The geometric reformulation follows by taking S = Spec V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−2}⟧ (ILO V 3.1.3); Remark 3.1.4 gives the equal-characteristic case from EQ.1/partial-algebraization-equal-characteristic.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p⟦x⟧ and the ideal (x − p), A′ = A works with S = Spec ℤ_p and Y = 𝔸¹_S.
The generic degree of A → A′ may be divisible by p but never by ℓ.

sources.locator: Exposé V, Théorème 3.1.1, Reformulation 3.1.3 and Remarque 3.1.4, p. 66 (printed)
sources.match: After a finite extension of generic degree prime to ℓ, a complete local normal mixed-characteristic ring becomes partially algebraizable for every finite family of ideals; geometrically it is the completion of a finite-type scheme over a regular complete base of dimension one less.

nodes.title: de Jong's equivariant nodal-curve alteration over an excellent base
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of excellent integral noetherian schemes and Z ⊂ X a nowhere dense closed subscheme, with η the generic point of Y, such that X_η is smooth, geometrically irreducible and of dimension 1 and Z_η is étale over η. There are a finite group G, a commutative square of G-schemes with f′ : X′ → Y′ over f, alterations a : X′ → X and b : Y′ → Y, an effective G-equivariant divisor D ⊂ X′ and a nowhere dense G-stable closed T′ ⊂ Y′ such that: f′ is projective; G acts trivially on X and Y and freely on Y′ − T′; a and b are projective generically étale alterations and Y′/G → Y (resp. X′/G → X) is an isomorphism at η (resp. at the generic point of X_η); f′ is a nodal curve, smooth outside T′; D is étale over Y′ and contained in the smooth locus of f′; and a^{-1}(Z) ⊂ D ∪ f′^{-1}(T′).
hypotheses: Y excellent integral noetherian; X_η smooth geometrically irreducible of dimension 1; Z_η étale over η.
A nodal curve is flat with geometrically connected one-dimensional fibres whose only singularities are ordinary double points.
proofSteps: Apply de Jong's Theorem 2.4 (Families of curves and alterations, 1997) to the triple (f, G = 1, Z): after an alteration of Y with group action and a stable-curve modification, the family becomes a projective semistable curve with disjoint sections through the smooth locus covering Z (de Jong 1997, 2.4 (i)–(vii)(a)); the extra boundary is T′ and the sections form D.
Read off the stated properties (ILO IX 1.2); the stable modification is also available from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.5/stable-modification-existence.
acceptance: If f is already a smooth projective curve with Z a union of disjoint sections, G trivial and a, b identities work.
For Y a trait and X a regular model with nodal special fibre, T′ is the closed point after base change.

The geometric hypothesis is necessary for the quotient conclusion: for a nontrivial finite separable extension L/K, ℙ¹_L → Spec K is smooth and irreducible but not geometrically irreducible. A nodal model with geometrically connected fibres has generic constants from its new base; compatibility with a birational quotient of ℙ¹_L would force the base quotient to have constants L, contradicting birationality over K.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.4 and Remark 2.5, pp. 602–603
sources.match: For a family of curves over an integral excellent base with a group action and a marked closed subset, there is an equivariant alteration making the family a projective semistable curve with smooth generic fibre and disjoint sections in its smooth locus through the marked set, with optional stability or birationality of the generic fibre. The birational quotient clause 2.4(iv) assumes geometric irreducibility (Situation 2.1.5).

sources.locator: Exposé IX, Théorème 1.2, p. 131 (printed)
sources.match: Records the weak form of de Jong's theorem used in the uniformization proofs: a projective nodal curve after an equivariant generically étale alteration, with the marked subset inside an étale divisor and the degenerate locus.

sources.locator: Théorème 1.2, p. 161
sources.match: The published theorem explicitly assumes geometric irreducibility of the generic fibre, correcting arXiv v1.

nodes.title: Gabber's weak local uniformization theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme and Z ⊂ X a nowhere dense closed subset. There is a finite family (X_i → X)_{i∈I}, covering for the alteration topology alt, such that each X_i is regular and connected and the preimage of Z in X_i is the support of a strict normal crossings divisor (possibly empty).
hypotheses: X noetherian quasi-excellent (possibly of infinite dimension; the statement is local); Z nowhere dense.
proofSteps: Reduce to X local, normal, complete of dimension d by EQ.0/uniformization-henselian-reduction and EQ.0/complete-local-reduction; argue by induction on d, the case d = 1 being normalisation (ILO VII 2.1–2.3).

Realise X (after a finite cover) as the completion of a finite-type relative curve X′ → S over a regular local S of dimension d − 1 at a closed point, with Z coming from a rare closed subset (EQ.1/partial-algebraization-mixed-characteristic, geometric form; EQ.1/partial-algebraization-equal-characteristic).

Apply EQ.2/de-jong-nodal-curve-alteration, uniformize the base by induction, and note that the resulting pair is log regular (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.4/log-regular-pair); resolve by Kato–Nizioł monoidal desingularization (PA.4/monoidal-desingularization; ILO VII 4.3).
acceptance: For X regular and Z an snc support, the identity family works.
For X the cone k[x, y, z]/(xy − z²) and Z the vertex, the blow-up of the vertex is an alt-covering family with regular source and exceptional divisor a smooth conic.

sources.locator: Exposé VII, Théorème 1.1 and §§2–4, pp. 81–83 (printed); Exposé II, Théorème 4.3.1, p. 33
sources.match: Gabber's weak local uniformization: a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme admits a finite alteration-topology covering by regular connected schemes on which a given rare closed subset becomes an snc support.

nodes.title: Gabber's prime-to-ℓ local uniformization theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, Z ⊂ X a nowhere dense closed subset and ℓ a prime invertible on X. There is a finite family (p_i : X_i → X)_{i∈I}, covering for the topology alt_ℓ′ of ℓ′-alterations, such that each X_i is regular and connected and p_i^{-1}(Z) is the support of a strict normal crossings divisor.
hypotheses: X noetherian quasi-excellent; ℓ invertible on X; Z nowhere dense.
proofSteps: Reduce to X complete local normal of dimension d by EQ.0/uniformization-henselian-reduction and EQ.0/complete-local-reduction, by induction on d (ILO IX 1).

Use the prime-to-ℓ partial algebraization (EQ.1/partial-algebraization-mixed-characteristic) and de Jong's equivariant nodal-curve alteration (EQ.2/de-jong-nodal-curve-alteration) with a group G; apply the induction hypothesis to Y′/H with H an ℓ-Sylow of G and use Abhyankar's lemma, reaching G an ℓ-group acting on log regular pairs (ILO IX 1.2–2.1, VI 1.9, 2.1).

Make the action very tame by Gabber's equivariant modification theorem (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.4/gabber-modification-absolute, ILO VIII 1.1), pass to the log regular quotient (PA.4/very-tame-quotient) and resolve it by monoidal desingularization (PA.4/monoidal-desingularization) (ILO IX 2.3).
acceptance: For ℓ not dividing any generic degree in the weak family, the weak uniformization family is already alt_ℓ′-covering.

For X the quotient 𝔸²/μ_ℓ by (x, y) ↦ (ζx, ζ^{-1}y) over a field of characteristic ≠ ℓ, the quotient map of degree ℓ is not allowed; the minimal resolution of the A_{ℓ−1} singularity is an alt_ℓ′-covering modification.

sources.locator: Exposé IX, Théorème 1.1 and §2 (Théorème 2.3), pp. 131–134 (printed); Exposé II, Théorème 4.3.2, p. 33; Exposé 0, Théorème 2
sources.match: Gabber's prime-to-ℓ uniformization: the alteration covering can be chosen of generic degrees prime to ℓ, with regular connected sources and snc boundary.

nodes.title: Hypercoverings by regular schemes with snc boundary
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, Z ⊂ X a closed subset with dense complement U, and N ≥ 0. There is a hypercovering ε : X_• → X for the alteration topology (resp. for alt_ℓ′ with ℓ invertible on X) such that for every i ≤ N the scheme X_i is regular (a finite disjoint union of regular connected schemes) and the preimage of Z in X_i is the support of a strict normal crossings divisor, so that U_i = U ×_X X_i is the complement of an snc divisor. The X_i may be chosen affine.
hypotheses: X noetherian quasi-excellent; Z rare; ℓ invertible on X for the alt_ℓ′ version; only the truncation in degrees ≤ N is controlled.
proofSteps: Deligne's inductive construction of hypercoverings (Hodge III §6.2): at each stage cover the relevant fibre product (cosk_n X_•)_{n+1}, an object of alt/X, by EQ.2/weak-local-uniformization (resp. EQ.2/prime-to-ell-local-uniformization) applied with the preimage of Z and of the degeneracy loci.
Zariski-refine each stage to affine pieces (ILO XIII 2.2.2, XV 3.1.2).
acceptance: For X regular with Z an snc support, the constant hypercovering X_• = X works.
The truncation level N must be at least q + 1 to control cohomology in degree q (ILO XIII 2.2.1–2.2.3).

sources.locator: Exposé XIII, Théorème 2.2.2, p. 196 (printed); Exposé XV, 3.1.2, p. 222 (printed)
sources.match: The local uniformization theorem with the standard hypercovering construction gives alteration hypercoverings whose first terms are regular with the preimage of a given closed subset an snc divisor.

nodes.title: Deligne's oriented product of topoi
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of topoi, with defining sites C_1, C_2, D having finite limits and f^*, g^* induced by continuous finite-limit-preserving functors. The oriented product X ←×_S Y is the topos of sheaves on the site C whose objects are triples (U → V ← W) with V ∈ D, U ∈ C_1, W ∈ C_2 and maps U → f^*V, g^*V ← W, with the topology generated by (a) coverings in the U variable, (b) coverings in the W variable, and (c) the maps (U → V′ ← W ×_V V′) → (U → V ← W) for V′ → V in D such that U → f^*V factors through f^*V′. It carries projections p_1 : X ←×_S Y → X, p_2 : X ←×_S Y → Y and a canonical 2-morphism τ : g p_2 ⇒ f p_1. For schemes it is applied to the étale topoi; for S a henselian trait, X_s ←×_S η is LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0's oriented product.
hypotheses: Sites with finite projective limits; coverings given by pretopologies; f^*, g^* continuous and left exact on sites.
proofSteps: Define the site and check the sheaf condition reduces to (a), (b) and bijectivity along (c) (ILO XI 1.1–1.2).
Construct p_1, p_2, τ and the universal property: morphisms T → X ←×_S Y correspond to triples (a, b, t) with t : g b ⇒ f a (ILO XI 1.3–1.7).
Points are triples (x, y, a specialization g(y) ⇝ f(x)); compare with the trait case of LPV.0/oriented-product-comparison.
acceptance: For S a point, X ←×_S Y = X × Y (product topos).
For X → S the identity of the étale topos of a strictly henselian trait and Y = η̄, the oriented product has the vanishing-topos description of LPV.0.

uses.how: the tube base change theorem for oriented products
oriented proper acyclicity and oriented cohomological descent
constructibility of Rj_* via generic constructibility and oriented descent

sources.match: Constructs Deligne's oriented product of topoi from a site of triples U → V ← W with three kinds of covering families, with its projections and 2-morphism, and identifies its points.

nodes.title: Base change for tubes of oriented products
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be coherent morphisms of coherent topoi, T = X ←×_S Y with projections p_1, p_2 and τ : g p_2 ⇒ f p_1, and Λ a ring. For every F ∈ D⁺(Y, Λ) the base change map f^*Rg_*F → Rp_{1*}p_2^*F deduced from τ is an isomorphism in D⁺(X, Λ).
hypotheses: X, Y, S coherent topoi and f, g coherent morphisms (SGA 4 VI).
proofSteps: T is coherent and p_1, p_2 are coherent (ILO XI Lemme 2.5).

Check the isomorphism on points of X; at a point x the stalk of Rp_{1*}p_2^*F is the cohomology of the tube over x, computed as a filtered colimit over neighbourhoods, which matches the stalk of f^*Rg_*F (ILO XI 2.4, proof).
acceptance: For S a point, the statement is the Künneth-free identity f^*Rg_*F = Rp_{1*}p_2^*F for the product with a point.
For schemes, at a geometric point x of X, the stalk is RΓ(Y ×_S S_(f(x)), F): cohomology of the 'Milnor tube' over the strict henselisation.

sources.locator: Exposé XI, Théorème 2.4 and Lemme 2.5, pp. 178–179 (printed)
sources.match: For coherent topoi and morphisms the base change map from f^*Rg_* to Rp_{1*}p_2^* of the oriented product is an isomorphism on bounded below complexes.

nodes.title: The oriented alteration topology on diagrams X → S ← Y
nodes.statement: Fix a noetherian base S₀. Let B be the category of diagrams (X → S ← Y) of finite-type S₀-schemes, with morphisms the commutative S₀-ladders; finite limits and finite coproducts in B are computed termwise. The oriented alteration topology on B is generated by the families: (i) (X → S ← Y_i) → (X → S ← Y) for an alteration covering (Y_i → Y); (ii) (X_i → S ← Y) → (X → S ← Y) for an alteration covering (X_i → X); (iii) (X ×_S S_i → S_i ← Y ×_S S_i) → (X → S ← Y) for an alteration covering (S_i → S); (iv) (X → S′ ← Y ×_S S′) → (X → S ← Y) for S′ → S proper through which X → S factors; (v) (X ×_S S′ → S′ ← Y) → (X → S ← Y) for S′ → S étale through which Y → S factors (ILO XII 2.1.1–2.1.2). An oriented alteration hypercovering of (X → S ← Y) is a simplicial object (X_• → S_• ← Y_•) of B whose degree-zero augmentation and all positive-degree matching maps are coverings for this topology; its augmentation induces ←ε : Y_• ←×_{S_•} X_• → Y ←×_S X.
hypotheses: All diagrams are finite type over a fixed noetherian S₀; covering families lie in this category. Each application may take S₀ to be its original base. Strict henselizations in stalk computations are handled by limits of étale neighbourhoods, not asserted to be objects of B.
proofSteps: Restrict the diagram category and the five generating families of ILO XII 2.1.1–2.1.2 to finite-type S₀-schemes. Finite limits remain noetherian and the families remain stable under base change. Arbitrary products of noetherian schemes need not be noetherian.
Define hypercoverings and the induced morphism of oriented products by functoriality (EQ.3/oriented-product-topos).
acceptance: A diagram with S = X and Y = X proper over S: the topology restricted to (i) is the alteration topology of X.
An alteration hypercovering S_• → S induces an oriented alteration hypercovering (X ×_S S_• → S_• ← Y ×_S S_•) (used in ILO XII 2.2.4).

uses.how: oriented cohomological descent along such hypercoverings
base change formula for alteration hypercoverings of the base

nodes.title: Oriented acyclicity of proper morphisms
nodes.statement: Let S be a coherent scheme, g : Y → S, π : S′ → S proper, a : X → S′ coherent, b = π a, Y′ = Y ×_S S′ with g′ : Y′ → S′ and ρ : Y′ → Y. The induced morphism ←ρ : Y′ ←×_{S′} X → Y ←×_S X of oriented products is acyclic for torsion sheaves: for every torsion abelian sheaf (more generally bounded below torsion complex) F on Y ←×_S X, F → R←ρ_* ←ρ^* F is an isomorphism. The companion assertion of 1-acyclicity for ind-finite stacks is recorded with proof gap NONABELIAN-ORIENTED-LIMIT; the abelian theorem does not depend on it.
hypotheses: π proper; coefficients torsion; schemes coherent.
proofSteps: Reduce by the tube base change theorem (EQ.3/tube-base-change) to a statement on strictly henselian local bases.

Apply ordinary proper base change for torsion sheaves to the strictly local fibre and use the section determined by the lifted geometric point to identify the adjunction map (ILO XII 1.2.1–1.2.2). Gabber’s affine proper base change is not needed for this step.
acceptance: For π an isomorphism, ←ρ is an equivalence.
This generalizes invariance of the tubular neighbourhood under admissible blow-ups (ILO XI 1.7, 2.8).

sources.locator: Exposé XII, Théorèmes 1.2.1–1.2.2 and §1.3.4, pp. 189–190 (printed)
sources.match: Proves torsion abelian acyclicity. The ind-finite-stack extension is stated separately in §1.3.4 with a warning about the limit argument, retained in the published version as §1.4.
The published discussion still identifies the missing reference for the non-abelian passage to limits.

nodes.title: Oriented cohomological descent
nodes.statement: Let (X_• → S_• ← Y_•) → (X → S ← Y) be a hypercovering for the oriented alteration topology, with augmentation ←ε : T_• = Y_• ←×_{S_•} X_• → T = Y ←×_S X. For every bounded below torsion complex K on T, the adjunction K → R←ε_* ←ε^* K is an isomorphism; the companion descent assertion for ind-finite stacks C, namely C → ←ε_* ←ε^* C, requires the limit input recorded in gap NONABELIAN-ORIENTED-LIMIT.
hypotheses: Diagrams finite type over a fixed noetherian S₀ as in EQ.3/oriented-alteration-topology; torsion coefficients; bounded below complexes.
proofSteps: By general descent theory (Deligne, Hodge III 5.3.5) reduce to 0-coskeleta of single covering families of types (i)–(v), and to Zariski coverings or proper surjections for the alteration coverings (ILO XII 2.3.1).

Type (iv) is EQ.3/oriented-proper-acyclicity; types (i), (ii), (v) follow from proper and étale cohomological descent (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.16) through the tube description; type (iii) combines them (ILO XII 2.3).
acceptance: For the constant hypercovering the statement is trivial.
For S_• → S the Čech nerve of a proper surjection S′ → S with X = S, Y = S, it recovers proper cohomological descent on S.

sources.locator: Exposé XII, Théorème 2.2.1 and §2.3, including §2.3.8, pp. 191–194 (printed)
sources.match: Proves oriented descent for bounded below torsion abelian complexes. Its non-abelian companion refers to the limit issue of §1.3.4, so it remains an explicit proof gap here.

nodes.title: Base change formula for alteration hypercoverings
nodes.statement: Let X —f→ S ←g— Y be finite-type morphisms of noetherian schemes and ε : S_• → S an alteration hypercovering, with f_• : X_• = X ×_S S_• → S_•, g_• : Y_• = Y ×_S S_• → S_• and ε_Y : Y_• → Y. For every bounded below torsion complex K on X, the natural map g^*Rf_*K → Rε_{Y*}(g_•^*Rf_{•*}(K|X_•)) is an isomorphism. The corresponding ind-finite-stack assertion g^*f_*C → ε_{Y*}(g_•^*f_{•*}(C|X_•)) remains conditional on gap NONABELIAN-ORIENTED-LIMIT.
hypotheses: S noetherian, X and Y of finite type over S; torsion coefficients. The noetherian source theorem is used here in this finite-type scope, which suffices for the applications to open and closed immersions.
proofSteps: Express both sides through oriented products with EQ.3/tube-base-change and apply EQ.3/oriented-cohomological-descent to the induced oriented hypercovering (EQ.3/oriented-alteration-topology) (ILO XII 2.4).
Typical use: Y = Z a closed subscheme of the base, so the restriction of Rj_* to Z is computed from the restrictions over a hypercovering (ILO XIII 2.2.3, XV 2.2.2).
acceptance: For S_• constant the map is the identity.
For X = U ⊂ S open, g : Z → S the closed complement and S_• regular with snc preimage of Z, the right side is computed from Rj_{•*}Λ, which absolute purity describes.

sources.locator: Exposé XII, Théorème 2.2.4 and §2.4, pp. 192–194 (printed)
sources.match: Base change of Rf_* along g can be computed after replacing the base by an alteration hypercovering and taking cohomological descent along the induced hypercovering of Y.

nodes.title: Constructibility of direct images via weak uniformization
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, f : Y → X a morphism of finite type, n ≥ 1 invertible on X and F a constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on Y. Then every R^q f_*F is constructible.
hypotheses: X noetherian quasi-excellent; n invertible on X; f of finite type; F constructible.
proofSteps: Classical reductions (SGA 4 XVI 4.5): to F = ℤ/ℓ constant (SGA 4 IX 2.14 and the trace method) and to f an open immersion j : U → X (ILO XIII 2.1.1–2.1.2).
By the constructibility criterion (SGA 4 IX 2.4 (v)) it suffices that for every closed immersion g : Z → X, g^*R^q j_*ℤ/ℓ is constructible over a dense open of Z.

Take an alteration hypercover X_• → X regular with snc preimage of the boundary X − U in degrees ≤ q + 1 (EQ.2/regular-alteration-hypercover). Absolute purity makes Rj_{p*}ℤ/ℓ constructible on X_p, hence so is its restriction to Z_p = Z ×_X X_p; no snc condition on the test-closed subset Z is required.

Apply Deligne’s generic constructibility over the noetherian base Z (SGA 4½ [Th. finitude] 1.9(i), p. 236) to the finite-type maps ε_p : Z_p → Z and the finitely many constructible cohomology sheaves needed in total degree q. These maps need not be proper. A common dense open of Z works, and oriented hypercover base change identifies the truncated descent complex with g^*Rj_*ℤ/ℓ (ILO XIII 2.2.3). The general-base supplier extension is requested from EDC.0.
acceptance: For X of finite type over a field this recovers Deligne's finiteness theorem of SGA 4½ for open immersions.
ILO XIX 2.2 gives an open immersion of noetherian (not quasi-excellent) schemes with R¹j_*ℤ/2 not constructible, so quasi-excellence cannot be dropped.

sources.locator: Exposé XIII, §2 (2.1–2.2, Théorème 2.2.2), pp. 195–197 (printed)
sources.match: Proves constructibility of the higher direct images using only weak local uniformization, absolute purity, Deligne's generic constructibility and oriented cohomological descent.

sources.locator: [Th. finitude] Théorème 1.9(i), p. 236; proof §2, pp. 238–241
sources.match: For finite-type X → Y over a noetherian S and a constructible torsion sheaf with invertible torsion, a dense base open has constructible, eventually vanishing higher direct images.

nodes.title: Gabber's finiteness theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, f : Y → X a morphism of finite type, n ≥ 1 invertible on X and F a constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on Y. Then (i) every R^q f_*F is constructible, and (ii) there is an integer N with R^q f_*F = 0 for q ≥ N. Equivalently Rf_* : D⁺(Y_ét, ℤ/n) → D⁺(X_ét, ℤ/n) carries D^b_c(Y_ét, ℤ/n) into D^b_c(X_ét, ℤ/n).
hypotheses: X noetherian quasi-excellent (possibly of infinite Krull dimension); n invertible on X.
proofSteps: Part (i) is EQ.4/constructibility-via-weak-uniformization; the proof of both parts at once proceeds by induction on c of the statement (P_c): for an open immersion j : U → X and K ∈ D^b_c(U), Rj_*K is constructible and bounded outside a closed subset of codimension > c (ILO XIII 3.1).

Inductive step: by prime-to-ℓ uniformization (EQ.2/prime-to-ell-local-uniformization) in the standard form of EQ.0/standard-form-covers (proper birational, Nisnevich, finite flat of degree prime to ℓ), compare the defect complexes ψ along the three kinds of maps; the finite flat step is split by the trace since the degree is prime to ℓ (ILO XIII 3.2–3.5).
On the regular schemes with snc boundary at the top, Rj_*Λ is constructible and bounded by absolute purity (ILO XIII 3.6.2); reduce from K to constant coefficients (ILO XIII 3.7).
acceptance: For f proper this is the proper finiteness theorem with no hypothesis on X.

For X = Spec of a strictly henselian regular local ring of dimension d and j the complement of an snc divisor with r branches, Rj_*ℤ/n has cohomology in degrees 0, …, r only (exterior algebra), in accordance with (ii).

sources.locator: Exposé XIII, Théorème 1.1.1, 1.1.2 and §3, pp. 195 and 198–204 (printed); Exposé 0, Théorème 1
sources.match: Gabber's finiteness theorem: for a finite-type morphism to a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme and torsion coefficients invertible on the base, higher direct images of constructible sheaves are constructible and vanish in large degrees.

nodes.title: Dimension functions
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian scheme. For points x, y of X with geometric points x̄, ȳ, a specialization x̄ ⇝ ȳ is an X-morphism X_(x̄) → X_(ȳ) of strict henselizations (equivalently an X-morphism x̄ → X_(ȳ)); it has codimension r if the closure in X_(ȳ) of the image of x̄ has dimension r. y is an étale immediate specialization of x if some x̄ ⇝ ȳ has codimension 1. A dimension function on X is a map δ : X → ℤ such that δ(y) = δ(x) − 1 whenever y is an étale immediate specialization of x. For a sheaf G on X, δ(G) = sup{δ(x) : G_x̄ ≠ 0} (−∞ for G = 0).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian; the notion depends only on X_red.
Sign convention: generizations have larger δ (as in ILO XIV 2.1.8 and XVII 2.1.1).
proofSteps: Definition (ILO XIV 2.1.1–2.1.2, 2.1.8); étale immediate specializations are detected on strict henselizations of the closure (ILO XIV 2.1.3) and, for quasi-excellent X, on the completion (ILO XIV 2.1.7).
acceptance: On a strictly henselian trait, δ(s) = 0, δ(η) = 1 is the dimension function vanishing at the closed point.

On 𝔸¹ over a trait R with uniformizer π, the closed point x = (πt − 1) is an immediate specialization of the generic point while dim of its closure is 0 and that of the generic point is 2; δ = dim of closure fails, δ = −dim O_{X,x} works.

uses.how: the affine Lefschetz bound δ_X(R^q f_*F) ≤ f^*δ_X(F) − q is phrased with dimension functions
potential dualizing complexes are pinned by Λ(δ(x))[2δ(x)] at every point
K_X lies in the heart of Gabber's perverse t-structure for the perversity −2δ
for finite-type schemes over a field the middle perversity uses δ(x) = dim of the closure of x, a dimension function

tests.name: DimensionFunction.test_trait
tests.statement: On a strictly henselian trait S with closed point s and generic point η, δ(s) = 0 and δ(η) = 1 define a dimension function, and every dimension function is δ + c for an integer c.

tests.name: DimensionFunction.test_field
tests.statement: On Spec k every function is a dimension function (there are no immediate specializations).

tests.name: DimensionFunction.test_affine_line_over_trait
tests.statement: On 𝔸¹_R over a trait R, x ↦ dim of the closure of x is not a dimension function: the closed point (πt − 1) has dimension 0 while the generic point has dimension 2 although the specialization is immediate; x ↦ −dim O_{X,x} is one.

tests.name: DimensionFunction.test_line_plane
tests.statement: For X the union of a line and a plane meeting at a point, x ↦ −dim O_{X,x} is not a dimension function (ILO XIV 2.2.3).

tests.name: DimensionFunction.test_finite_type_field
tests.statement: For X of finite type over a field, x ↦ dim of the closure of x is a dimension function and agrees with EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5/point-dimension-function.

api.name: DimensionFunction
api.statement: The set of dimension functions on X, as functions X → ℤ.

api.name: DimensionFunction.etaleRestrict
api.statement: Composition with an étale U → X gives a dimension function on U; dimension functions on étale X-schemes form an étale sheaf.

api.name: DimensionFunction.sub_locallyConstant
api.statement: The difference of two dimension functions is locally constant; dimension functions form a torsor under locally constant ℤ-valued functions wherever one exists.

api.name: DimensionFunction.ofStrictLocal
api.statement: For X strictly local, noetherian and universally catenary, δ(t) = dim closure{t} is the normalized dimension function with δ(closed point) = 0 (ILO XIV 2.4.5). This applies to strictly local quasi-excellent schemes by XIV 2.4.4.

api.name: DimensionFunction.negCodim
api.statement: On an integral universally catenary X, x ↦ −dim O_{X,x} is a dimension function (ILO XIV 2.2.2).

api.name: DimensionFunction.ofFiniteType
api.statement: On X of finite type over a field or over ℤ, or local universally catenary, x ↦ dim of the closure of x is a dimension function (ILO XIV 2.4.5).

api.name: DimensionFunction.supSheaf
api.statement: δ(G) for a sheaf G, with δ(G) ≤ δ(H) when G is a subquotient of H.

sources.locator: Exposé XIV, Définitions 2.1.1–2.1.2 and 2.1.8, Remarque 2.2.3, Corollaire 2.4.5, pp. 209–216 (printed); Exposé XVII, Définition 2.1.1, p. 263
sources.match: Defines specializations of geometric points, their codimension, étale immediate specializations, and dimension functions as integer functions dropping by one along every étale immediate specialization, with examples and a non-example.

nodes.title: Existence of dimension functions
nodes.statement: (1) (Gabber) A noetherian scheme is universally catenary if and only if it admits a dimension function Zariski-locally. (2) (Gabber) Every quasi-excellent scheme admits dimension functions étale-locally, and they form an étale torsor under the sheaf of locally constant ℤ-valued functions. (3) On a normal quasi-excellent scheme, x ↦ −dim O_{X,x} is a dimension function.
hypotheses: Noetherian (1); quasi-excellent (2), (3).
proofSteps: (1) ⇒: on an integral universally catenary scheme −dim O is a dimension function, and the local choices on components glue on an open neighbourhood (ILO XIV 2.2.2, 2.2.4). ⇐: a dimension function forces catenarity (ILO XIV 2.2.5), and then Ratliff's theorem on formal catenarity of henselian local rings gives universal catenarity (ILO XIV 1.2.2, 1.3.1, 2.2.6).
(3) for normal quasi-excellent X: the henselisation is quasi-excellent and universally catenary (ILO XIV 1.3.2) and unibranch, so Zariski and étale immediate specializations agree (ILO XIV 2.3.3).
(2) glue over irreducible components étale-locally (ILO XIV 2.3.2) and reduce to normal integral X via the normalisation (ILO XIV 2.3.4–2.3.5).
acceptance: Nagata's catenary but not universally catenary local domain (EGA IV 5.6.11, ILO XIV 2.6) has no dimension function Zariski-locally, by (1).
A strictly henselian trait is excellent and has dimension functions globally.

sources.locator: Exposé XIV, Théorèmes 2.2.1 and 2.3.1, Propositions 2.2.2, 2.2.6, 2.3.3, pp. 212–214 (printed)
sources.match: A noetherian scheme is universally catenary iff it has dimension functions Zariski-locally; quasi-excellent schemes have them étale-locally; −dim of the local ring is one on normal quasi-excellent schemes.

nodes.title: Dimension functions induced along finite-type and regular morphisms
nodes.statement: Let δ_X be a dimension function on a noetherian scheme X. (1) For f : Y → X of finite type, δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) + trdeg(κ(y)/κ(f(y))) is a dimension function on Y (written f^*δ_X). (2) For f : Y → X a regular morphism of excellent schemes, δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) − dim O_{Y_{f(y)}, y} is a dimension function on Y.
hypotheses: (1) f of finite type, X noetherian with a dimension function; (2) f regular (flat with geometrically regular fibres) between excellent schemes.
proofSteps: (1) Reduce to X, Y integral and f dominant; X is universally catenary by EQ.5/dimension-function-existence, so δ_X = −dim O_X + const, and the dimension formula (Matsumura 14.C) gives δ_Y = −dim O_Y + trdeg(κ(Y)/κ(X)) + const (ILO XIV 2.5.1–2.5.2).

(2) Reduce to a local regular map between strictly local excellent schemes. The regular fibres are universally catenary. On each fibre the difference between the displayed function and an existing dimension function is locally constant; regular base change on H⁰ shows that these fibres are connected in this strictly local situation. The difference therefore descends to X, where the Hauptidealsatz makes it constant along immediate specializations (ILO XIV 2.5.3–2.5.4, pp. 217–218).
acceptance: For f : 𝔸¹_k → Spec k with δ = 0 on the base, (1) gives δ(η) = 1 and δ(closed point) = 0.
For the completion map Spec Â → Spec A of an excellent local ring with δ(closed point) = 0, (2) gives the dimension function of Spec Â vanishing at its closed point.

sources.locator: Exposé XIV, Proposition 2.5.1, Corollaire 2.5.2 and Proposition 2.5.4, pp. 216–218 (printed); Exposé XVII, Propositions 4.1.1–4.1.2, p. 280
sources.match: A dimension function induces one along a finite-type morphism by adding the transcendence degree of the residue extension, and along a regular morphism of excellent schemes by subtracting the dimension of the local ring of the fibre.

nodes.title: Base change along regular morphisms
nodes.statement: Consider a cartesian square T′ = T ×_S S′ with f : T → S quasi-compact and quasi-separated, g : S′ → S a regular morphism of noetherian schemes, f′ : T′ → S′ and g′ : T′ → T. For n invertible on S and every sheaf F of ℤ/n-modules on T, the base change map g^*Rf_*F → Rf′_*g′^*F is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: g regular between noetherian schemes; f qcqs; n invertible on S.
proofSteps: Popescu: write S′ as a filtered limit of smooth S-schemes S_i (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.15).
Smooth base change (SGA 4 XVI 1.2; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.2) along each S_i → S and passage to the limit in étale cohomology (SGA 4 VII 5.11; SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.15) (ILO XIV 2.5.3).
acceptance: For A strictly henselian excellent local and an open U ⊆ Spec A, regular base change evaluated at the closed point identifies H^q(U,F) with H^q(U ×_A Â,F). Strict locality is needed for this global-cohomology deduction (ILO XV 1.2.5).
For g smooth this is smooth base change.

Without henselianity global cohomology can change: over A = k[t]_(t), char k ≠ 2, the étale cover z² = 1+t has no section over A but has a section over k⟦t⟧. The regular-base-change sheaf assertion is unaffected.

sources.locator: Exposé XIV, Lemme 2.5.3, pp. 216–217 (printed)
sources.match: Base change along a regular morphism of noetherian schemes is an isomorphism for torsion coefficients invertible on the base, by Popescu's theorem, smooth base change and passage to the limit.

nodes.title: Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem over a trait
nodes.statement: Let S be a trait with the dimension function δ_S(η) = 1, δ_S(s) = 0, X a scheme of finite type over S with the induced dimension function δ_X (EQ.5/induced-dimension-function), f : Y → X an affine morphism of finite type and n invertible on S. For every constructible sheaf F of ℤ/n-modules on Y and every q, δ_X(R^q f_*F) ≤ f^*δ_X(F) − q. In particular, for a strictly local scheme X′ essentially of finite type over S of dimension d and an affine open U ⊂ X′, H^q(U, ℤ/n) = 0 for q > d.
hypotheses: S a trait (henselian is the case used); X of finite type over S; n invertible on S.
proofSteps: Gabber's proof (1994), written in Illusie, Perversité et variation, Manuscripta Math. 112 (2003), §2, Théorème 2.4: reduce to an open immersion and constant coefficients, alter X by de Jong's semistable alteration over the trait, compute Rj_* on strictly semistable models by absolute purity, and descend (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.20; LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §0.10).
The essentially-finite-type local statement follows by passage to the limit (ILO XV 3.3.2).
acceptance: For X of finite type over a field (the closed fibre), this is the affine Lefschetz theorem SGA 4 XIV 3.1 (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.4/affine-vanishing-hypercohomology).
For X = S strictly henselian and f the (affine) inclusion of the generic point η, R¹f_*ℤ/n is the skyscraper ℤ/n(−1) at s, with δ = 0 = δ(η) − 1, so the bound is attained.

planet.name: Gabber's affine Lefschetz over a trait

sources.locator: Exposé XV, Remarque 1.1.3 and §3.3.2, pp. 219 and 224 (printed), citing Illusie 2003, 2.4
sources.match: Records that Gabber proved the affine Lefschetz inequality for schemes of finite type over a trait (written in Illusie 2003) and uses its strictly local, essentially finite-type form as the base case of the general theorem.

nodes.title: Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-excellent scheme with a dimension function δ_X, f : Y → X an affine morphism of finite type and n invertible on X. For every constructible sheaf F of ℤ/n-modules on Y and every q, δ_X(R^q f_*F) ≤ f^*δ_X(F) − q, where f^*δ_X is the induced dimension function of EQ.5/induced-dimension-function. Equivalently, for X strictly local quasi-excellent with δ_X(t) = dim of the closure of t, H^q(Y, F) = 0 for q > f^*δ_X(F).
hypotheses: X quasi-excellent with a dimension function; f affine of finite type; n invertible on X; F constructible.
proofSteps: Reformulate stalkwise at geometric points and reduce to the strictly local statement; reduce to an affine open immersion and constant coefficients by SGA 4 XIV 4.4 and the trace method (ILO XV 1.2.1–1.2.4).
Reduce to X complete by regular base change along the completion (EQ.5/regular-base-change, ILO XV 1.2.5).

Take an alteration hypercovering X_• with regular terms and snc boundary in degrees ≤ N (EQ.2/regular-alteration-hypercover); by absolute purity, the cohomology of U depends only on the combinatorics of the boundary along the closed fibre (ILO XV 2.1.7, 2.2.2–2.2.4, via EQ.3/alteration-hypercover-base-change).

Approximate X_• over the henselisation of an affine space over a Cohen ring by Popescu (EQ.0/artin-popescu-approximation), keeping regularity and combinatorics; specialise along a section close to the identity to a scheme essentially of finite type over a trait, and conclude by EQ.5/gabber-trait-affine-lefschetz (ILO XV 3).
acceptance: For X = Spec k (k separably closed) this is Artin vanishing H^q(Y, F) = 0 for q > dim Supp F on affine Y.
For X a strictly henselian regular local scheme of dimension 2 and U = X − V(f), H^q(U, ℤ/n) = 0 for q > 2.

sources.locator: Exposé XV, Théorème 1.1.2 and §§1.2–3, pp. 219–224 (printed); Exposé 0, Théorème 7
sources.match: Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem: for an affine finite-type morphism to a quasi-excellent scheme with a dimension function, the q-th direct image of a constructible sheaf is supported in δ-dimension at most the δ-dimension of the sheaf minus q.

nodes.title: Local form of the affine Lefschetz theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a strictly local quasi-excellent scheme of dimension d, U ⊂ X an affine open and n invertible on X. Then H^q(U, ℤ/n) = 0 for q > d. More generally, for X henselian local quasi-excellent of dimension d with residue field k and ℓ invertible on X, cd_ℓ(U) ≤ d + cd_ℓ(k) for every affine open U; if X is integral with fraction field K, cd_ℓ(K) = d + cd_ℓ(k).
hypotheses: X quasi-excellent; strictly local (first statement) or henselian local (second).
proofSteps: Equivalent to EQ.5/affine-lefschetz-theorem for open immersions and constant coefficients (ILO XV 1.2.3–1.2.4).
For henselian X combine with the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence over the residue field (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.15); the lower bound for K is SGA 4 X 2.5 (ILO Exposé 0, Corollaire 8).
acceptance: For X = Spec of a strictly henselian trait and U = η, H^q(η, ℤ/n) = 0 for q > 1 (the tame inertia is ℓ-cohomologically of dimension 1).
For X = Spec W(k̄)⟦x⟧ with k̄ algebraically closed (d = 2) and U = X[1/p], H^q(U, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for q > 2.

sources.locator: Exposé XV, Corollaire 1.2.2 and Corollaire 1.2.4, p. 220 (printed); Exposé 0, Corollaire 8, p. 5
sources.match: For a strictly local quasi-excellent scheme of dimension d, affine opens have cohomological dimension at most d; for henselian ones the bound is d plus that of the residue field, with equality for the fraction field.

nodes.title: Gabber's bound on cohomological dimension
nodes.statement: Let X be a strictly local noetherian scheme of dimension d > 0 and ℓ a prime invertible on X. For every open U ⊂ X, cd_ℓ(U) ≤ 2d − 1. Consequently, if X is integral with fraction field K then cd_ℓ(K) ≤ 2d − 1; and for f : X′ → Y of finite type with Y noetherian of finite dimension, Rf_* has finite ℓ-cohomological dimension.
hypotheses: X noetherian strictly local, not necessarily quasi-excellent; ℓ invertible.
proofSteps: Punctured spectrum: by Gabber's formal base change (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.8/open-henselian-completion) pass to the completion, which is excellent; cover U = X − {x} by d principal opens X_{f_i} and use the Čech spectral sequence with EQ.5/affine-lefschetz-local to get H^i(U, F) = 0 for i ≥ 2d (ILO XVIII-A Lemme 2.1).
Coniveau spectral sequence: H^i_Y(X, F) = 0 for i > sup_{y∈Y}(cd_ℓ(κ(y)) + 2 dim O_{X,y}) (ILO XVIII-A Lemme 2.2).

Induction on d using the restriction from U to dense opens V and the inductive bound for residue fields (ILO XVIII-A §2); the corollaries follow by limits and by the Čech reduction to affine f (ILO XVIII-A 1.2, 1.4).
acceptance: For d = 1 (strictly henselian trait), cd_ℓ(η) ≤ 1.
Infinite-dimensional noetherian bases are excluded from the finiteness of cd(Rf_*); for X of finite dimension the bound complements EQ.4/gabber-finiteness-theorem (ii).

sources.locator: Exposé XVIII-A, Théorème 1.1, Corollaires 1.2 and 1.4, Lemmes 2.1–2.2, pp. 331–334 (printed)
sources.match: Gabber's bound: open subsets of a strictly local noetherian scheme of dimension d > 0 have ℓ-cohomological dimension at most 2d − 1, with consequences for fraction fields and finite-type direct images.

nodes.title: Transition morphisms for specializations
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 2, Λ = ℤ/n and X be noetherian excellent over ℤ[1/n]. For K ∈ D⁺(X_ét,Λ), write RΓ_x̄(K) for cohomology on X_(x̄) with supports in its closed point. A specialization ȳ ⇝ x̄ of codimension c = 0 or 1 gives a natural map sp : RΓ_ȳ(K) → RΓ_x̄(K)(c)[2c] in D⁺(Λ). For c = 0 it is transport along the corresponding geometric-point isomorphism. On a strictly henselian trait, first project the generic stalk to its wild-inertia invariants K_η̄^S (averaging is available for the invertible torsion coefficients); the tame-inertia evaluation construction then gives the codimension-one map independently of the generator. For an integral one-dimensional strict localization, use its normalization and multiply the trait map by 1/[s̃:s], the inverse purely inseparable residue degree. Closed-support adjunction gives the map for every immediate specialization. Higher-codimension transitions will be constructed on cohomology groups in EQ.6/top-degree-local-class; no derived map in arbitrary codimension is asserted.
hypotheses: X noetherian excellent over ℤ[1/n] (quasi-excellent suffices étale-locally, ILO XVII 3.1.3); Λ = ℤ/n.
proofSteps: On a strictly henselian trait compute RΓ_s(K) by the complex F(K) of XVII 1.2.2.1. The map from K_η̄(−1) first uses K_η̄ → K_η̄^S and then tame evaluation; the generator-change homotopy makes the induced derived map independent of the choice (1.2.3.1–1.2.3.2, pp. 260–262).

For an integral strictly local excellent curve normalize to a strictly henselian trait and insert the factor 1/[s̃:s] (1.3.1, p. 262). For an immediate specialization on X use the closure of the generizing point and i^! (1.4.1).

Codimension-zero transport and immediate maps compose when the total codimension is at most one (1.4.2, p. 263). The higher group maps and their general composition law belong to the joint induction of 3.1.1–3.1.2 in the subsequent node.
acceptance: On a strictly henselian trait with K = Λ, the derived map Λ → RΓ_s(Λ(1))[2] induces the Kummer isomorphism Λ → H²_s(Λ(1)).
For c = 0 (an isomorphism of strict localizations) sp is the identity.

uses.how: potential dualizing complexes require pinnings compatible with sp for immediate specializations
existence and uniqueness of potential dualizing complexes glue local pinnings along sp

tests.statement: On a strictly henselian trait, sp_{η̄→s}(Λ) : Λ → H²_s(X, Λ(1)) is an isomorphism, matching the Kummer boundary of a uniformizer.

tests.name: TransitionMorphism.test_identity
tests.statement: For the identity specialization (c = 0), sp is the identity of RΓ_x̄(K).

tests.name: TransitionMorphism.test_wild_projection
tests.statement: On a trait with residue characteristic p ≠ ℓ, let a finite p-quotient of wild inertia act on an ℓ-primary generic stalk M with M^S = 0. The transition for j_!M vanishes. This detects omission of the averaging projection M → M^S.

tests.statement: For K = i_{s*}Λ supported at the closed point of a trait, RΓ_η̄(K) = 0 so sp vanishes, although RΓ_s(K) = Λ ≠ 0.

api.name: TransitionMorphism.comp
api.statement: Immediate and codimension-zero derived maps compose when the total codimension is at most one. For arbitrary total codimension the cohomology-group composition law is the joint theorem EQ.6/top-degree-local-class (ILO XVII 3.1.2).

api.name: TransitionMorphism.finite
api.statement: For finite maps, compatibility of immediate transitions with the trace, including the inseparable residue-degree normalization (ILO XVII 3.3.1).

api.name: TransitionMorphism.trait
