sources.locator: Exposé XVII, §§1.2–1.4, especially Définitions 1.2.3.1, 1.3.1, 1.4.1 and Remarque 1.4.2, pp. 260–263 (printed)
sources.match: Constructs derived transitions in codimensions zero and one. Remarque 1.4.2 explicitly reserves the higher-codimension construction for cohomology groups only.

nodes.title: Higher transitions and top-degree local cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be a normal strictly henselian excellent local ℤ[1/n]-scheme of dimension d with closed point x. Then H^q_x(X, Λ(d)) = 0 for q > 2d, and there is an isomorphism [x] : Λ → H^{2d}_x(X, Λ(d)) compatible with the transition morphisms of immediate specializations. Jointly, for every noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme, K ∈ D⁺(X_ét,Λ) and specialization ȳ ⇝ x̄ of codimension c, there are natural group maps sp : H^i_ȳ(K) → H^{i+2c}_x̄(K(c)), extending the codimension-zero and codimension-one derived transitions. They compose along specializations and commute with finite trace. These are maps of cohomology groups; the theorem makes no arbitrary-codimension derived-map assertion.
hypotheses: For the top class X is normal strictly local excellent of dimension d; for group transitions X is any noetherian excellent scheme. In both cases Λ = ℤ/n with n invertible.
proofSteps: Use the affine Lefschetz cohomological bounds for vanishing above 2d (ILO XVII 3.2). Prove the top-class generator in dimension two by resolving an excellent surface and computing the exceptional-curve cohomology with absolute purity (§3.4).

Construct arbitrary-codimension group transitions by chains of immediate specializations. The surface computation and connectedness arguments give independence of the chain and finite-map compatibility (§3.5). This is part of the simultaneous induction proving Theorems 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, rather than an invocation of the final top-class theorem in the immediate-transition construction.

For higher-dimensional normal strict local X, coniveau and the lower-dimensional classes show that [x] generates H^{2d}_x (§3.6.2). Formal base change reduces injectivity to complete X. Embed complete X in a regular complete local scheme using Cohen structure; exceptional pullback of the already constructed regular potential complex supplies the putative pinnings and their immediate compatibility (2.4.4.1). The normal-scheme lemma Λ ≅ τ_{≤0}K and the transition square force [x] to be injective (§3.6.3–3.6.4, pp. 279–280). This uses the regular case, not general existence of potential dualizing complexes.
acceptance: For X regular, [x] is the fundamental class of the closed point given by absolute purity.
For d = 1 (a strictly henselian trait), [x] is the Kummer class Λ → H²_x(Λ(1)).

For a regular strictly henselian surface and constant Λ, two successive immediate maps on cohomology give Λ → H⁴_x(Λ(2)), the absolute-purity isomorphism; different saturated chains give the same group map.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Théorèmes 3.1.1–3.1.2 and §§3.2–3.6, pp. 268–280 (printed)
sources.match: Jointly proves the top-degree local class and all-codimension cohomology-group transitions, with independence of chains, composition and finite-trace compatibility.

nodes.title: Putative and potential dualizing complexes
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ. A putative dualizing complex is K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) together with, for every x ∈ X, an isomorphism (pinning) RΓ_x(K) ≅ Λ(δ(x))[2δ(x)] in D⁺(x_ét, Λ). It is a potential dualizing complex if for every immediate specialization ȳ → x̄ the pinnings at y and x are compatible with sp_{ȳ→x̄} : RΓ_ȳ(K) → RΓ_x̄(K)(1)[2] (EQ.6/transition-morphism), using δ(y) = δ(x) + 1.
hypotheses: X noetherian excellent over ℤ[1/n]; δ a dimension function; Λ = ℤ/n.
proofSteps: Definition (ILO XVII 2.1.2). Étale restriction and quasi-finite exceptional pullback transport putative structures (2.2.1, 2.4.3.1). For f finite surjective, a putative K is potential iff f^!K with its induced pinnings is potential (2.4.3.3). Finite pushforward does not preserve rank-one pinnings: two points over a point would give Λ².
acceptance: On a strictly henselian trait with δ(s) = 0, δ(η) = 1, K = Λ(1)[2] with the Kummer pinning at s is potential.
Λ on the same trait is not putative for this δ.

uses.how: existence and uniqueness up to unique isomorphism on excellent schemes with a dimension function
a potential dualizing complex is dualizing
(μ_ℓ^{⊗d})[2d] on a strictly henselian excellent regular local ring is the normalised dualizing complex

tests.statement: On Spec k with δ ≡ 0, K = Λ with the identity pinning is potential; with δ ≡ 1 it is Λ(1)[2].

tests.statement: On a strictly henselian trait with δ(s) = 0, δ(η) = 1, K = Λ(1)[2]: RΓ_η̄(K) = Λ(1)[2] and RΓ_s(K) ≅ Λ by Kummer theory, compatibly with sp.

tests.name: PotentialDualizing.test_empty

tests.statement: For X separated of finite type over a field with δ(x) = dim of the closure of x, a^!Λ (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1:adjoint/dualizing-complex) with its purity pinnings is potential.

api.statement: f^*K is potential for the induced δ_Y when f is regular between excellent schemes (ILO XVII 4.1.1).

api.statement: f^!K is potential for f^*δ when f is of finite type and compactifiable (ILO XVII 4.1.2).

api.statement: Two potential dualizing complexes for the same (X, δ) are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism respecting the pinnings (ILO XVII 5.1.1).

api.name: PotentialDualizing.mem_perv
api.statement: K lies in the heart of Gabber's perverse t-structure for the perversity −2δ.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Définition 2.1.2 and §2.2–2.4, pp. 263–267 (printed)
sources.match: A putative dualizing complex is pinned at every point by Λ(δ(x))[2δ(x)]; it is potential when the pinnings are compatible with the transition morphisms of immediate specializations.

nodes.title: The constant sheaf on a regular scheme is potentially dualizing
nodes.statement: Let X be a regular excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with the dimension function δ = −codim. The constant sheaf Λ, with the pinnings RΓ_x(Λ) ≅ Λ(−c)[−2c] (c = codim x) given by absolute cohomological purity and the fundamental classes, is a potential dualizing complex.
hypotheses: X regular excellent over ℤ[1/n]; δ(x) = −dim O_{X,x}.
proofSteps: The pinnings exist by absolute purity for the regular immersion of the closure of x near x (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §0.10; ILO XVI 3.1.1).

Compatibility with sp for an immediate specialization ȳ → x̄: work on X_(x̄); with C the closure of ȳ and C̃ its normalisation (a strictly henselian trait), reduce via i^! and the finite map C̃ → C to the trait case (ILO XVII 2.4.2.1, 2.4.3.3–2.4.3.4).
acceptance: For X a strictly henselian trait, this is the Kummer pinning of Λ at the closed point and the trivial pinning at η.
For X smooth over a field, the pinnings agree with the smooth-pair cycle classes of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.3.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Propositions 2.4.1.1, 2.4.2.1 and 2.4.4.1, pp. 264–267 (printed)
sources.match: On a regular excellent scheme with dimension function minus the codimension, the constant sheaf with its absolute-purity pinnings is a potential dualizing complex.

nodes.title: Gabber's perverse t-structures for a perversity function
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian scheme and p : X → ℤ ∪ {+∞} a perversity function: p(x) ≥ p(y) for every specialization ȳ → x̄ of geometric points. The pair (D^{≤p}, D^{≥p}) with K ∈ D^{≤p}(X_ét, Λ) iff K|_x ∈ D^{≤p(x)}(x_ét, Λ) for all x, and K ∈ D^{≥p} iff RΓ_x(K) ∈ D^{≥p(x)}(x_ét, Λ) for all x, is a t-structure on D⁺(X_ét, Λ). Its heart Perv^p(X, Λ) is a stack for the étale topology: objects and morphisms glue.
hypotheses: X noetherian; p monotone along specializations; Λ = ℤ/n.
proofSteps: Use Gabber’s weak-perversity construction, valid for noetherian X with p monotone under specialization. Iteratively modify a Godement resolution by the sheaf of sections with supports in the specialization-closed families determined by p; the depth estimates and truncation arguments give orthogonality and the truncation triangle (G04 §§4–6, pp. 3–8). This construction covers perversities that do not come from a finite constructible stratification.

Stalk and local-support conditions are étale-local, so restriction is t-exact. Descent for derived étale sheaves together with vanishing of negative Hom between heart objects makes the heart an ordinary étale stack (ILO XVII 5.2.1, p. 287). Proposition 5.2.2 concerns pseudo-open immersions and perverse adjoints, not stack descent.

For the finite-type-field middle-perversity comparison use the owner’s EDC.5 contract. Constructibility requires its separate hypotheses; G04 §8, Théorème 8.2, pp. 10–12 treats the constructible restriction. No general constructibility assertion for an arbitrary p is made.
acceptance: For X a point and p ≡ 0 this is the standard t-structure.
For X a strictly henselian trait and δ(s) = 0, δ(η) = 1, Λ(1)[2] lies in Perv^{−2δ} while Λ does not.

uses.how: uniqueness of the potential dualizing complex and Λ ≅ τ_{≤0}RHom(K_X, K_X) use K_X ∈ Perv^{−2δ} and étale gluing in the heart
perverse sheaves over traits use a rectified dimension function, a case of these perversities

api.statement: Étale pullback is t-exact for the restricted perversity.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, §5.2.1, p. 287 (printed)
sources.match: Recalls the pointwise t-structure and the étale-stack property of its heart. The construction itself is read in G04.
Builds the pointwise t-structure for weak perversities using supported Godement resolutions and proves the constructible restriction under additional hypotheses.

nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of potential dualizing complexes
nodes.statement: Let X be an excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ. Then (X, δ) admits a potential dualizing complex K_X, unique up to unique isomorphism preserving all pinnings, the canonical map Λ → τ_{≤0}RHom(K_X, K_X) is an isomorphism, and K_X ∈ Perv^{−2δ}(X, Λ).
hypotheses: X noetherian excellent over ℤ[1/n] with a global dimension function.
proofSteps: Uniqueness and the τ_{≤0} statement: two potential dualizing complexes lie in Perv^{−2δ} and isomorphisms between them form an étale sheaf with a unique section compatible with pinnings (EQ.6/gabber-perverse-t-structure; ILO XVII 5.2–5.3).

For normal X, let j : U → X be a dense regular open. With the normalized generic dimension, use the perverse extension T = j_*^φΛ for φ(x) = max(0, 2 codim(x) − 2). The localization triangle and the top local class identify its stalks and local supports with the prescribed pinnings; compatibility with immediate transitions proves potentiality (ILO XVII 5.3.1). Twists and shifts handle other dimension functions.

For general reduced X use finite normalization X̃ → X and a closed complement Z of the normal locus. Combine the potential complexes on X̃, Z and X̃ ×_X Z by the explicit cone construction of XVII 5.4.1; finite-surjective shriek detection verifies the pinnings and their compatibility. Nilpotents do not change the étale topos. Étale descent in the perverse heart glues the resulting local objects. This is not a claim that pushing a potential complex forward along normalization preserves it.
acceptance: For X regular with δ = −codim, K_X = Λ (EQ.6/regular-potential-dualizing).
For X separated of finite type over a field with δ = dim of closure, K_X = a^!Λ.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Théorème 5.1.1 and §§5.3–5.4, pp. 287–293 (printed)
sources.match: On an excellent scheme with a dimension function a potential dualizing complex exists, is unique up to unique isomorphism, has τ_{≤0}RHom(K, K) = Λ and lies in the heart for the perversity −2δ.

nodes.title: Functoriality of potential dualizing complexes
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ_X and K a putative (resp. potential) dualizing complex. (1) For f : Y → X a regular morphism of excellent schemes and δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) − codim_{f^{-1}(f(y))}(y), f^*K is naturally putative (resp. potential) on (Y, δ_Y). (2) For f : Y → X of finite type and compactifiable and δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) + trdeg(κ(y)/κ(f(y))), f^!K is naturally putative (resp. potential) on (Y, δ_Y). Both constructions are compatible with composition.
hypotheses: Excellent noetherian schemes over ℤ[1/n]; f regular in (1), compactifiable of finite type in (2).
proofSteps: (1) Pinnings pull back by regular base change for local cohomology (EQ.5/regular-base-change) and absolute purity of the regular fibres (ILO XVII 4.2.1–4.2.3).
(2) Reduce to f smooth (smooth purity, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2:trace-purity/smooth-purity) and f a closed immersion (quasi-finite i^!) (ILO XVII 4.1.2 and §4.3).
acceptance: For f étale, (1) and (2) both give the restriction of K with the restricted δ.
For f : 𝔸¹_X → X, (2) gives f^!K = f^*K(1)[2] with δ_Y = δ_X + 1 at generic points of fibres.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Propositions 4.1.1–4.1.2, Remarque 4.1.3 and §4.2, pp. 280–284 (printed)
sources.match: Putative and potential dualizing complexes pull back along regular morphisms and under exceptional pullback along compactifiable finite-type morphisms, with the induced dimension functions.

nodes.title: Dualizing complexes on noetherian schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian ℤ[1/n]-scheme and Λ = ℤ/n. A dualizing complex on X is an object K ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) such that the duality functor D_K = RHom(−, K) preserves D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) and, for every L ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ), the biduality morphism L → D_K D_K L is an isomorphism. (Unlike SGA 5 I 1.7, finite quasi-injective dimension is not required.)
hypotheses: X noetherian over ℤ[1/n]; constructible bounded complexes.
proofSteps: Definition (ILO XVII 0.8). For two dualizing objects, comparison of the two duality equivalences makes their difference tensor-invertible (7.5.1.1, pp. 308–309). For Λ = ℤ/n apply self-injectivity and finite-module biduality to each prime-power factor and then the Chinese remainder decomposition.
acceptance: Λ on Spec of a separably closed field is dualizing.
For X finite type over a field, a^!Λ is dualizing (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1:biduality/constructible-biduality).

uses.how: Gabber's duality theorem asserts existence on excellent schemes with a dimension function
the dualizing complex (μ_ℓ^{⊗d})[2d] on a regular local ring and its restriction to an open are used with Rj_* D = D j_! and local duality

tests.name: IsDualizingComplex.test_point
tests.statement: On Spec of a separably closed field, Λ = ℤ/n is dualizing: D_Λ is Λ-linear duality on finite complexes and Λ is self-injective.

tests.name: IsDualizingComplex.test_double
tests.statement: On the same point, Λ ⊕ Λ is not dualizing: D D Λ = Hom(Λ², Λ²) = Λ⁴ ≠ Λ.

tests.name: IsDualizingComplex.test_empty
tests.statement: On the empty scheme 0 is dualizing.

tests.name: IsDualizingComplex.test_finite_type
tests.statement: For X separated of finite type over a field, the complex a^!Λ of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1:adjoint/dualizing-complex is dualizing in this sense.

tests.name: IsDualizingComplex.test_composite_shifts
tests.statement: At a geometric point with Λ = ℤ/6, L = 𝔽₂ ⊕ 𝔽₃[1] is invertible with inverse 𝔽₂ ⊕ 𝔽₃[−1]. Tensoring a dualizing object with L remains dualizing, although L is not Λ[k] for a single k.

api.name: IsDualizingComplex
api.statement: The predicate on K ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ).

api.name: IsDualizingComplex.dual
api.statement: D_K = RHom(−, K) as a contravariant endofunctor of D^b_c(X_ét, Λ).

api.name: IsDualizingComplex.biduality
api.statement: L ≅ D_K D_K L for constructible L.

api.name: IsDualizingComplex.restrictOpen
api.statement: For j : U → X open, j^*K is dualizing and Rj_* RHom_U(F,j^*K) ≅ RHom_X(j_!F,K). The latter follows from extension-by-zero tensor compatibility and j_! ⊣ j^*; biduality gives preservation and open restriction (ILO XVII 7.6.3, p. 311). This general-base formal interface is requested from EDC.1.

api.name: IsDualizingComplex.unique
api.statement: Two dualizing complexes differ by tensoring with an invertible object (ILO XVII 7.5.1.1). Étale-locally an invertible object has one rank-one shifted factor Λ_ℓ[k_ℓ] for each prime-power factor Λ_ℓ = ℤ/ℓ^{v_ℓ(n)}; the shifts can differ with ℓ. A single local form Λ[k] is valid for prime-power n, not for arbitrary composite n (XVII 9.1–9.2).

api.name: IsDualizingComplex.sga5
api.statement: For a potential dualizing complex on a noetherian excellent scheme with dimension function, finite quasi-injective dimension holds iff X has finite Krull dimension; in that case it satisfies the stronger SGA 5 definition (ILO XVII 6.1.1). This criterion is stated with those geometric hypotheses.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Définition 0.8, p. 257 (printed)
sources.match: A dualizing complex is a constructible bounded complex whose duality functor preserves constructible bounded complexes and satisfies biduality; finite quasi-injective dimension is not imposed.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Proposition 7.5.1.1, pp. 308–309; Proposition 7.6.3, p. 311; Propositions 9.1–9.2, pp. 323–324
sources.match: Provides uniqueness via an invertible object, open restriction/formal exchange, and the componentwise shifted rank-one description of invertibles over general coefficient rings.

nodes.title: Biduality for potential dualizing complexes
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ and K the potential dualizing complex of (X, δ). Then K ∈ D^b_ctf(X_ét, Λ); K has finite quasi-injective dimension iff X has finite Krull dimension; D_K = RHom(−, K) preserves D^b_c(X_ét, Λ); and for every M ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) the biduality morphism M → D_K D_K M is an isomorphism. Thus K is a dualizing complex.
hypotheses: X noetherian excellent over ℤ[1/n] with a dimension function.
proofSteps: Constructibility, Tor-dimension and quasi-injective dimension of K and of D_K M from Gabber's finiteness theorem (EQ.4/gabber-finiteness-theorem) and change of coefficients (ILO XVII 6.2).

Weak reflexivity M ≅ τ_{≤0} D D M for constructible sheaves (ILO XVII 6.3.1) and reduction to finite-type schemes over bases of smaller dimension, generalising SGA 4½ [Th. finitude] 4.3 (ILO XVII 6.4.2).

Induction on dimension: reduce to M = j_!Λ for a dense open immersion of normal integral schemes and use the partial algebraization theorem (EQ.1/partial-algebraization-mixed-characteristic, geometric form V 3.1.3) to compare with the completion of a finite-type scheme over a regular base of smaller dimension (ILO XVII 6.5).
acceptance: For X of finite type over a field or over a regular base of dimension ≤ 1, this is SGA 4½ [Th. finitude] 4.3 (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1:biduality/constructible-biduality, one-dimensional-dualizing-base).
For X = Spec of a strictly henselian regular local ring of dimension d, K = Λ(d)[2d] (δ(closed point) = 0) and biduality holds for j_!Λ with j the complement of a divisor.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Théorème 6.1.1 and §§6.2–6.5, pp. 293–300 (printed)
sources.match: The potential dualizing complex of an excellent scheme with a dimension function is constructible of finite Tor dimension, its duality preserves constructible complexes and satisfies biduality; it has finite quasi-injective dimension exactly in finite Krull dimension.

nodes.title: Gabber's duality theorem on excellent schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme admitting a dimension function. Then X has a dualizing complex K, unique up to tensoring with an invertible object; K ∈ D^b_ctf(X_ét, Λ), and K has finite quasi-injective dimension iff X has finite Krull dimension. Moreover: if X is regular, Λ is a dualizing complex; if f : Y → X is flat with geometrically regular fibres and Y noetherian excellent, f^*K is dualizing; if f : Y → X is of finite type and compactifiable, f^!K is dualizing.
hypotheses: X noetherian excellent over ℤ[1/n] with a dimension function (necessary: a dualizing complex forces a global dimension function, Gabber 2004 Lemma 8.1).
proofSteps: Existence: the potential dualizing complex (EQ.6/potential-dualizing-existence) is dualizing (EQ.6/gabber-biduality-theorem).
Uniqueness up to invertible objects (ILO XVII 7.5.1.1, 9.2).
Regular case: EQ.6/regular-potential-dualizing; functoriality: EQ.6/potential-dualizing-functoriality with EQ.6/gabber-biduality-theorem on Y.
acceptance: For X a strictly henselian regular local scheme, Λ and Λ(d)[2d] are both dualizing and differ by the invertible object Λ(d)[2d].
For X of finite type over a field, K = a^!Λ up to an invertible object.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Théorème 0.9, p. 257 (printed) (cited as Théorème 0.2 by Česnavičius–Scholze, following the Astérisque numbering); Exposé 0, (c), p. 6
sources.match: Gabber's theorem: an excellent noetherian scheme with a dimension function has a dualizing complex, unique up to invertible objects, Λ is dualizing on regular schemes, and dualizing complexes pull back along regular morphisms and under exceptional pullback.

nodes.title: The normalised dualizing complex of a regular local ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian excellent regular local ring of dimension d with closed point x, ℓ a prime invertible in R, Λ = ℤ/ℓ, and δ(t) = dim of the closure of t. Then K = (μ_ℓ^{⊗d})[2d] = Λ(d)[2d] is the potential dualizing complex of (Spec R, δ), pinned at x by RΓ_x(K) ≅ Λ through absolute purity; for every open immersion j : U → Spec R, j^!K = K|_U is dualizing on U, and Rj_* ∘ D_U ≅ D_X ∘ j_! on constructible complexes.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian, excellent, regular local; ℓ invertible.
proofSteps: δ = d − codim, so the potential dualizing complex for δ is Λ(d)[2d] by EQ.6/regular-potential-dualizing and the shift rule PotentialDualizing.shift; the pinning at x is H^{2d}_x(Λ(d)) ≅ Λ by absolute purity (ILO XVI 3.1.1).

It is dualizing by EQ.6/gabber-biduality-theorem; restriction to an open is j^* = j^! (SGA 4 XVIII 3.1.8 (iii)), and Rj_* D_U = D_X j_! is the formal adjunction (SGA 5 I 1.12 (a); EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1:adjoint/formal-duality-exchange).
acceptance: For d = 1 (a strictly henselian DVR), K = Λ(1)[2], recovering the dimension-one dualizing base of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1:biduality/one-dimensional-dualizing-base.
For d = 0 (a separably closed field), K = Λ.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.2.3, p. 33
sources.match: Uses that (μ_ℓ^{⊗dim R})[2 dim R] is dualizing on a strictly henselian excellent regular local ring, normalised by absolute purity, that its restriction to an open is dualizing, and that Rj_* exchanges with duality and j_!.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, Théorème 0.9 and Proposition 2.4.4.1, pp. 257 and 267 (printed); Exposé XVI, Théorème 3.1.1
sources.match: Provides the regular case of the duality theorem and the purity normalisation.

nodes.title: Local duality on strictly local excellent schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be a strictly local noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with closed point x, and K a dualizing complex on X pinned at x by RΓ_x(K) ≅ Λ (the potential dualizing complex for δ with δ(x) = 0). For every F ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) and every i there is a natural isomorphism H^i_x(X, F) ≅ Hom_Λ(H^{−i}(D_K F)_x̄, Λ).
hypotheses: X strictly local excellent; Λ = ℤ/n with n invertible; F constructible bounded.
proofSteps: Biduality F ≅ D_K D_K F (EQ.6/gabber-biduality-theorem).
Apply i_x^!: RΓ_x(X, F) ≅ RΓ_x RHom(D_K F, K) ≅ RHom_Λ((D_K F)_x̄, i_x^!K) ≅ RHom_Λ((D_K F)_x̄, Λ), using i_x^! RHom(G, K) = RHom(i_x^*G, i_x^!K) and the pinning.
Λ = ℤ/n is self-injective (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1:biduality/self-injective-coefficients), so cohomology commutes with Hom into Λ (SGA 5 I (4.2.2)).
acceptance: For X = Spec of a separably closed field this is linear duality of finite Λ-modules.
For X a strictly henselian trait, F = Λ and K = Λ(1)[2]: H²_x(Λ) ≅ Hom(H^{−2}(Λ(1)[2])_x̄, Λ) = Λ(−1), as Kummer theory predicts.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.2.3, p. 33, citing SGA 5 I (4.2.2) and ILO XVI 3.1.1
sources.match: Invokes local duality for the dualizing complex normalised by absolute purity to turn vanishing of stalks of RHom(j_!ℤ/ℓ, K) into vanishing of local cohomology.

sources.locator: Exposé XVII, §6 (Le théorème de dualité locale), Théorème 6.1.1, p. 293 (printed)
sources.match: Supplies the biduality from which the local duality isomorphism follows.

nodes.title: Local absolute purity for finite étale coefficients
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a regular local ring and G a commutative finite étale R-group scheme whose order is invertible in R. Then H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < 2 dim R.
hypotheses: R regular local (not necessarily excellent); |G| invertible in R.
proofSteps: By the local-to-global spectral sequence for supports reduce to strict henselizations. Compare cohomology with supports with that of the maximal-ideal completion using CS24 Lemma 3.1.2 (AT.8/open-henselian-completion). The completed regular local ring is excellent, so absolute purity applies with no missing excellence assumption on the original R.

Absolute cohomological purity for the regular closed point x ∈ Spec R of codimension d = dim R: Ri_x^!ℤ/n ≅ ℤ/n(−d)[−2d] (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §0.10, Riou's proof of Gabber's theorem), so H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/n) = 0 for i ≠ 2d.
Česnavičius–Scholze give a second proof by tilting (EQ.8/tilting-supports) to equal characteristic, where SGA 4 XVI 3.7 applies (CS24 3.1.3 proof).
acceptance: For R a DVR, H⁰_𝔪 = H¹_𝔪 = 0 and H²_𝔪(R, μ_n) ≅ ℤ/n.
For R = k⟦x, y⟧ with k separably closed, H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < 4 and H⁴_𝔪 ≅ ℤ/ℓ(−2).

sources.locator: Theorem 3.1.3, p. 30; announced as Theorem 1.1.2, p. 3
sources.match: For a regular local ring and a commutative finite étale group of invertible order, cohomology with supports in the closed point vanishes below twice the dimension (Gabber–Thomason purity).

sources.locator: Exposé XVI, Théorème 3.1.1 (Riou)
sources.match: Absolute cohomological purity for regular closed immersions of regular schemes.

nodes.title: Sheafified local purity with the cycle class
nodes.statement: Let R be a regular local ring of dimension d and n invertible in R. The étale sheafifications ℋ^i_𝔪(−, ℤ/n) of local cohomology at the closed point vanish for i ≠ 2d, and the cycle class map ℤ/n(−d) → ℋ^{2d}_𝔪(−, ℤ/n) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: R regular local; n invertible.
proofSteps: This is absolute purity for the regular immersion of the closed point (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §0.10), with the fundamental class of the point.
Česnavičius–Scholze note that their tilting argument reduces it to positive characteristic after proving injectivity of the cycle class map as in Fujiwara 2002, Lemma 2.3.1 (CS24 3.1.4).
acceptance: For d = 1 the isomorphism is the Kummer boundary ℤ/n(−1) ≅ H²_𝔪(ℤ/n) on the strict henselisation.
The vanishing statement for i < 2d is EQ.7/local-absolute-purity for G = ℤ/n.

sources.locator: Remarks 3.1.4, p. 31
sources.match: Notes that the perfectoid argument also reduces full absolute purity, including the cycle class isomorphism in degree twice the dimension, to positive characteristic.

nodes.title: Vanishing for principal punctured opens
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian excellent regular local ring of dimension d, f ∈ 𝔪 and ℓ a prime invertible in R. Then H^i(Spec R[1/f], ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i > d.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian excellent regular local, dim R = d, f ∈ 𝔪 and ℓ invertible in R.
proofSteps: Apply EQ.5/affine-lefschetz-local directly to the affine open Spec R[1/f] of the excellent strictly local scheme Spec R. If f = 0 the open is empty and the conclusion is immediate. In CS24 Lemma 3.2.3 this bound is used after completion, when excellence is automatic; no comparison of this punctured-open cohomology for an arbitrary R with its maximal-ideal completion is asserted.
acceptance: For d = 1 and f a uniformizer, Spec R[1/f] is the generic point and H^i = 0 for i > 1.
For f a unit, Spec R[1/f] = Spec R and H^i = 0 for i > 0, consistent with the bound.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.2.3, equation (3.2.3.2), p. 33; Lemma 3.1.2, p. 30
sources.match: Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem gives vanishing of the cohomology of R[1/f] above dim R for a strictly henselian complete regular local ring, and Lemma 3.1.2 passes to the completion.

nodes.title: Local cohomology of extension by zero from a principal open
nodes.statement: Let R be a regular local ring of dimension d, f ∈ 𝔪, ℓ a prime invertible in R and j : Spec R[1/f] → Spec R. Then H^i_𝔪(R, j_!ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < d.
hypotheses: R regular local; f ∈ 𝔪; ℓ invertible.
proofSteps: Reduce to strictly henselian R and apply the supported clause of CS24 Lemma 3.1.2 to the constructible sheaf j_!ℤ/ℓ and the maximal-ideal completion. This compares H^i_𝔪(R,j_!ℤ/ℓ) with the same supported cohomology on the complete regular local ring; it does not first compare H^i(R[1/f],ℤ/ℓ). If f = 0 then j_!ℤ/ℓ = 0. Otherwise the complete ring is excellent and the remaining duality argument applies.

With K = Λ(d)[2d] (EQ.6/regular-local-dualizing-complex), D(j_!Λ) = Rj_*(K|_U), whose stalk at the closed point is RΓ(R[1/f], Λ(d)[2d]); by EQ.7/punctured-affine-vanishing, H^{−i}(D(j_!Λ))_x̄ = 0 for −i + 2d > d, i.e. for i < d.
Local duality (EQ.6/local-duality) gives H^i_𝔪(R, j_!Λ) ≅ Hom(H^{−i}(D(j_!Λ))_x̄, Λ) = 0 for i < d.
acceptance: For d = 1 and f a uniformizer, H⁰_𝔪(R, j_!ℤ/ℓ) = 0.
For f a unit, j_!ℤ/ℓ = ℤ/ℓ and the statement is weaker than EQ.7/local-absolute-purity.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.2.3, equation (3.2.3.1), p. 33
sources.match: Reduces the local Lefschetz statement to vanishing of local cohomology of j_!ℤ/ℓ below dim R, and proves it by duality from the affine Lefschetz vanishing for R[1/f].

nodes.title: Lefschetz hyperplane theorem in local étale cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a regular local ring, f ∈ 𝔪 and ℓ a prime invertible in R. The restriction map H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) → H^i_𝔪(R/(f), ℤ/ℓ) is bijective for i < dim R − 1 and injective for i = dim R − 1.
hypotheses: R regular local of dimension d; f ∈ 𝔪 (R/(f) need not be regular); ℓ invertible.
proofSteps: The exact sequence 0 → j_!ℤ/ℓ → ℤ/ℓ → i_*ℤ/ℓ → 0 for i : Spec R/(f) → Spec R gives a long exact sequence of local cohomology with H^i_𝔪(R, i_*ℤ/ℓ) = H^i_𝔪(R/(f), ℤ/ℓ).
By EQ.7/extension-by-zero-local-vanishing, H^i_𝔪(R, j_!ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < d, which gives the bijectivity for i < d − 1 and injectivity for i = d − 1.
acceptance: For d = 1 (a DVR) and f a uniformizer, the statement is injectivity of H⁰_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 → H⁰(R/(f), ℤ/ℓ) = ℤ/ℓ in degree 0 = d − 1.

With EQ.7/local-absolute-purity, for R = R̃/(f) a hypersurface quotient of a regular R̃ of dimension d, H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < d − 1 (the hypersurface case of CS24 3.2.4, consumed by PurityForFlatCohomology PF.1).

sources.locator: Lemma 3.2.3 and its proof, p. 33
sources.match: For a regular local ring, f in the maximal ideal and ℓ invertible, local cohomology with ℤ/ℓ coefficients restricts bijectively to R/(f) below dim R − 1 and injectively in degree dim R − 1.

nodes.title: Matched punctured opens of a henselian perfectoid pair and its tilt
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, A a ring and ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p such that A is ϖ-henselian with bounded ϖ^∞-torsion and its ϖ-adic completion Â is (integral) perfectoid. Put A^♭ = lim_{a ↦ a^p} A/ϖA (the tilt of Â) and choose ϖ^♭ ∈ A^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ. The isomorphism A^♭/ϖ^♭ ≅ Â/ϖ = A/ϖ (the unpowered consequence of CS24 (2.1.2.2)–(2.1.2.3)) identifies Spec(A/ϖ) with Spec(A^♭/ϖ^♭). A matched pair of punctured opens is a pair (U, U^♭) of opens Spec A[1/ϖ] ⊆ U ⊆ Spec A and Spec A^♭[1/ϖ^♭] ⊆ U^♭ ⊆ Spec A^♭ whose closed complements, subsets of V(ϖ) and V(ϖ^♭), correspond under this identification. U ↦ U^♭ is an order isomorphism between the two sets of such opens.
hypotheses: ϖ^p | p; A ϖ-henselian with bounded ϖ^∞-torsion; Â perfectoid; ϖ^♭ chosen with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ.
proofSteps: The supplier Q5 gives A^♭/(ϖ^♭)^p ≅ Â/ϖ^p. Frobenius gives isomorphisms from Â/ϖ to Â/ϖ^p and from A^♭/ϖ^♭ to A^♭/(ϖ^♭)^p; composing the latter with the sharp-quotient map and the inverse of the former gives the unpowered quotient isomorphism (CS24 2.1.2.2–2.1.2.3). Bounded torsion gives Â/ϖ ≅ A/ϖ. The quotient spectra identify the closed subsets of V(ϖ) and V(ϖ^♭), and taking complements gives the order isomorphism.
acceptance: (Spec A, Spec A^♭) and (Spec A[1/ϖ], Spec A^♭[1/ϖ^♭]) are matched.
For k = 𝔽̄_p and A = W(k)⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − x) (p-adically completed) and ϖ = x^{1/p}, A^♭ ≅ k⟦t^{1/p^∞}⟧ and Spec A/ϖ is a point, so only these two pairs exist.

uses.how: idempotents and étale cohomology of U and U^♭ are identified
cohomology with supports in a closed Z ⊂ Spec A/ϖ is the cone of restriction to U = Spec A − Z

nodes.title: Multiplicative tilting of the generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let A be perfectoid and ϖ-adically complete for ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p, and ϖ^♭ ∈ A^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ. The p-power inverse limits satisfy compatible multiplicative bijections lim_{a↦a^p}(A[1/ϖ]) ≅ A^♭[1/ϖ^♭] and lim_{a↦a^p} A ≅ A^♭, the second being the multiplicative description of the tilt.
hypotheses: A perfectoid, ϖ-adically complete; ϖ^p | p.
proofSteps: The image Ā of A in A[1/ϖ] is p-integrally closed (PerfectoidQuotients Layer 0 p-integral closedness criterion with the decomposition along ϖ-torsion (2.1.3.1)).

A p-power compatible sequence in A[1/ϖ] therefore has ϖ^N times its terms in Ā for one N; combine with lim_{a↦a^p} A ≅ A^♭ (PerfectoidQuotientsPartII Q5/tilt-inverse-limit-monoid) after inverting ϖ^♭ (CS24 (2.1.7.2)).
acceptance: For a mixed-characteristic perfectoid field C and A = 𝒪_C, choose ϖ with ϖ^p | p. The assertion identifies C^♭ with lim_{x↦x^p} C as multiplicative monoids; it makes no identification of C itself with C^♭.
For A of characteristic p (A = A^♭), both maps are the identity.

sources.match: p-integral closedness of the image of a perfectoid ring in its generic fibre gives the multiplicative identification of the p-power limit of A[1/ϖ] with A^♭[1/ϖ^♭], compatibly with that of A with A^♭.

nodes.title: Tilting of idempotents on punctured opens
nodes.statement: In the setting of EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens, for every matched pair (U, U^♭) there is a bijection Idem(U) ≅ Idem(U^♭) between the idempotents of Γ(U, O) and of Γ(U^♭, O), compatible with orthogonality and functorial in A and U.
hypotheses: As in EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens.
proofSteps: Replace A by its ϖ-adic completion; idempotents of U do not change (Bouthier–Česnavičius 2.3.1; equivalently H⁰ of ℤ/2 under ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.8/open-henselian-completion).
For U = Spec A and U = Spec A[1/ϖ], idempotents are fixed by p-th powers, so the multiplicative bijections of EQ.8/punctured-multiplicative-tilt restrict to bijections of idempotents.

General U: an idempotent on U is an idempotent on A[1/ϖ] with compatible idempotents on the localisations along principal opens of U ∩ V(ϖ); by Beauville–Laszlo glueing these localisations may be completed; their completions are perfectoid with the matching tilts (PerfectoidQuotients Layer 0, Corollary 2.1.6 and (2.1.2.2)), reducing to the two settled cases.
acceptance: For A connected and U = Spec A, Idem = {0, 1} on both sides.
For A = A_1 × A_2, the idempotents (1, 0), (0, 1) correspond to those of A_1^♭ × A_2^♭.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.2.7 and its proof (first part), pp. 21–22
sources.match: Identifies the idempotents of an open between the generic fibre and the whole spectrum with those of the matched open of the tilt, compatibly with orthogonality, by p-th power limits and Beauville–Laszlo glueing.

nodes.title: Étale cohomology of products of valuation rings and their tilts
nodes.statement: Let A = ∏_{i∈I} V_i with each V_i a ϖ-adically complete valuation ring of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction field, over a perfectoid base as in EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens. Then A is perfectoid with A^♭ = ∏ V_i^♭; for every quasi-compact open U ⊆ Spec A (resp. U^♭ ⊆ Spec A^♭) there are no nonsplit étale covers; RΓ_ét(U, G) and RΓ_ét(U^♭, G) are concentrated in degree 0, given by locally constant G-valued functions; and for matched (U, U^♭) they are identified functorially through EQ.8/tilting-idempotents.
hypotheses: V_i complete of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction fields; G a torsion abelian group.
proofSteps: The V_i are perfectoid, products of perfectoids are perfectoid with tilt the product of tilts (PerfectoidQuotients Layer 0 products; PerfectoidQuotientsPartII Q6/tilting-valuation-rings).

Connected components of Spec ∏ V_i are the spectra of ultraproducts, which are valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.3/product-components); quasi-compact opens therefore have strictly henselian local rings and no nonsplit étale covers (CS24 Lemma 2.2.4).
Locally constant functions are determined by the Boolean algebra of clopens, which the idempotent bijection identifies compatibly with disjointness.
acceptance: For I a singleton, A = V and U = Spec V[1/ϖ] = Spec of an algebraically closed field: RΓ = G in degree 0 on both sides.
For I infinite, the clopens of Spec ∏ V_i correspond to subsets in ultrafilters, identically on the tilt.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.2.4, pp. 19–20, and proof of Theorem 2.2.7 (product case), pp. 21–22
sources.match: Products of valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields have quasi-compact opens with no nonsplit étale covers, so their étale cohomology is locally constant functions, matched under tilting by the idempotent bijection.

nodes.title: Algebraic tilting of étale cohomology
nodes.statement: In the setting of EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens, for every matched pair (U, U^♭) and every torsion abelian group G there is an isomorphism RΓ_ét(U, G) ≅ RΓ_ét(U^♭, G), functorial in A, U and G.
hypotheses: As in EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens; G torsion.
proofSteps: Replace A by its completion (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.8/open-henselian-completion).

By formal glueing for étale cohomology (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.8/formal-glueing) and ϖ-complete arc descent (CS24 Theorem 2.2.5; AT.11/complete-etale-hyperdescent), reduce to U = Spec A and U = Spec A[1/ϖ].

Products of complete valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields form a basis of the ϖ-complete arc topology (AT.11/complete-valuation-product-basis), matched with the analogous basis of A^♭ by tilting (PerfectoidQuotientsPartII Q6/tilting-valuation-rings, AT.12/tilting-complete-arc-covers); conclude from EQ.8/valuation-product-tilting by descent.
acceptance: For A of characteristic p, A^♭ = A and the isomorphism is the identity.

For R̂_∞ = W(k)⟦x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f) and U the complement of V(x_1, …, x_d), the cohomology of U equals that of the corresponding punctured spectrum of the f-adic completion of k⟦(x_1^♭)^{1/p^∞}, …⟧ (the step used in CS24 3.1.3).

sources.locator: Theorem 2.2.7 and its proof, pp. 21–22; Theorem 2.2.5, p. 20
sources.match: Étale cohomology with torsion coefficients of an open between the generic fibre and the spectrum of a henselian perfectoid pair agrees with that of the matched open of the tilt, by ϖ-complete arc descent to products of valuation rings.

nodes.title: Tilting of cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: In the setting of EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens, for every closed Z ⊆ Spec(A/ϖA) and every torsion abelian group G, RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_{Z^♭}(A^♭, G), where Z^♭ ⊆ Spec(A^♭/ϖ^♭) corresponds to Z.
hypotheses: As in EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens.
proofSteps: Apply EQ.8/tilting-etale-cohomology to the matched pairs (Spec A, Spec A^♭) and (Spec A − Z, Spec A^♭ − Z^♭) and take cones in the cohomology-with-supports triangle (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.0/cohomology-with-supports).
acceptance: For Z = ∅ both sides vanish.
For A = R̂_∞ as in CS24 3.1.3 and Z the closed point, it identifies H^i_{(p, x_1, …, x_d)}(R̂_∞, ℤ/ℓ) with local cohomology of the tilt.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.2.7, equation (2.2.7.1), p. 21
sources.match: Cohomology with supports in a closed subset of Spec(A/ϖ) agrees with that of the tilt, by the supports triangle.
